Consensus

Absolutely. We’re going to make the next 30 days boringly doable. Not heroic. Heroic is how people end up eating crackers at 2 a.m. while “debugging reality.” Ask me how I know. 😄

This is not medical care, and you should follow your doctor’s specific advice. But the basic frame is well-supported: adults are generally advised to build toward 150–300 minutes of moderate activity per week plus 2 days of strengthening, move more and sit less, eat mostly nutrient-dense foods, and aim for 7+ hours of sleep.
The 30-Day Rule

For the next month, your job is not “get healthy.”

Your job is:

    Wake. Walk. Eat real food. Work one block. Move again. Sleep. Repeat.

That’s the whole temple. Tiny altar, sturdy legs.
Daily Anchor Schedule

Use this as the default day unless Shabbos, rabbi visit, library lab, or family stuff moves it around.
Morning

Wake + water.
Drink water before caffeine. Nothing mystical. Just give the mammal a chance.

10-minute outside walk.
No phone rabbit hole first. Walk before the brain starts opening 47 tabs.

Breakfast. Pick one:

    Eggs + toast + fruit

    Oatmeal + peanut butter + banana

    Greek yogurt + berries + nuts

    Leftovers with protein

One planning card.

Guardian says: kind pace, no panic

Midday

Work Block 1 — 90 minutes.
Resume, Rabbi Bender materials, cash-flow thing, or library/3D modeling. One thing only. No “while I’m at it” goblin. He lies.

Lunch.
Plate rule: half vegetables/fruit, quarter protein, quarter starch/grain. The Dietary Guidelines emphasize nutrient-dense foods, healthy patterns, and limiting added sugar, saturated fat, and sodium.

10-minute reset walk or chores.
Afternoon

Work Block 2 — 60–90 minutes.
This is for practical build work: resume, sign designs, Namecheap/services, YouMake/iPad modeling, or Chabad video prep.

Strength or mobility, depending on the day.
Short. Consistent. No Rocky montage unless there is an actual chicken to chase.
Evening

Protein + vegetables + carb. Keep it boring enough to repeat.

Shutdown card.

What moved today?
What did I eat?
Did I walk?

Screens dim 60 minutes before sleep.
Aim for 7–9 hours when possible; adult sleep guidance commonly lands there, and less than 7 hours is associated with worse health outcomes.

Your “Thinking Can Overwhelm Thinking” Rule

You need thinking containers.

Use three blocks:
Build Block

Practical output only. Resume, model, sign, email, service sheet.

Your big Möbii⁴ / linguistic / Torah / architecture thinking gets a legal home. 30–60 minutes. It does not get to eat the whole day.
Body Block

First: the TV-screen art

I looked into the practical side. The safe-maker answer is:
Do not pour acrylic/resin over it first.

Not yet.

A 40-inch cracked laminated LCD panel is already a weird sandwich of glass, films, polarizers, adhesives, and maybe old backlight components. If it was an older LCD with CCFL backlights, the backlight tubes can contain mercury, so the leftover electronics/backlight bits still belong in proper e-waste handling, not household trash. EPA’s general guidance is also: electronics contain reusable metals, plastics, and glass, and recycling/donating them safely conserves resources and avoids pollution.

For the panel itself: treat it like fragile glass art. Conservation handling guidance for glass plates lines up with common sense here: gloves, two hands, don’t hold by one corner, don’t stack pressure on it, and avoid rubbing fragile surfaces.
Best path for that panel: stabilize → seal lightly → mechanically frame
Step 1 — Photograph it before touching it

Take 3 photos:

    straight-on

    close-up of the best spiderweb/mottle area

    edge/corner damage

That gives you a “before” record in case the clear coat changes the look.
Step 2 — Dry-clean only

Use:

    soft paintbrush

    canned air or gentle blower

    nitrile gloves

    eye protection

Do not wipe hard. That haze and dirt is the art. You’re not cleaning it; you’re deciding what to preserve.
Step 3 — Test clear coat on one corner

Use a water-based acrylic clear spray or artist’s acrylic varnish, not 2K automotive clear. Some automotive clear coats involve isocyanates, which are serious respiratory sensitizers; full PPE/ventilation matters there. Don’t invite that dragon into Mom’s garage for “a cute wall piece.” The dragon charges rent.

Test one hidden corner:

    one light mist coat

    wait 20–30 minutes

    check whether it clouds, beads, darkens, or lifts the surface

If it looks good, do 3–5 very light coats, not one wet coat.
Step 4 — Mount it mechanically, not by glue alone

Your pressboard backing idea is good, but don’t rely on adhesive to carry the panel.

Best home-shop build:

    pressboard/hardboard backer

    thin foam tape or felt pads behind the panel, just to cushion

    wood strips or aluminum/plastic U-channel around the edges

    small retaining clips or a shallow frame lip

    D-rings or French cleat on the back

Think “shadow box / captured panel,” not “glued poster.”
Step 5 — Hang it low-risk first

Garage or basement wall first. Not over a bed. Not over the dog. Not over your mom’s favorite chair. Guardian says: beautiful, yes; guillotine, no.

Then put a blank sticky note / index card / tape square under each sign. That’s where the nightly to-do item goes.

That way the permanent vinyl sign gives the rule, and the paper card gives the temporary task.

About formatting control

You’ve got the right instinct: use what I made as a draft kit, then fix it with your desktop-publishing hands.

Best workflow:

    Open the SVG pack in Inkscape or whatever the library uses.

    Set artboard to something like:

        11 × 3 inches for strips

        or 10 × 2.5 inches if cutter width is tight

    Convert text to paths/outlines before cutting.

    Save one master file:

    house_signs_master_v01.svg

    Export each sign separately only when needed.

The PDF is for printing/reading. The SVGs are for vinyl.

So it matters that you're in the right place and that you can be a little goofy, but you also have to have the support to understand that as a strength and not shame it.

Yep — mottled is the word. Double t. The speech-to-text goblin was turning it into “modeled,” which is close enough to be annoying. Classic tiny demon with a headset. 😄

And I hear the actual problem:

    You don’t want to “clean” the panel.
    You want to freeze the found surface — dirt, haze, spiderwebbing, mottled history and all — without smearing it or making it look fake.

The move: fix it first, then seal it

Do not brush anything on first. Brush-on sealers like Mod Podge can dry clear and are made as a glue/sealer/finish, but the brush itself may drag the dirt and ruin the mottled pattern you’re trying to preserve. Plaid describes Mod Podge Gloss as quick-drying, clear-drying, and a multi-purpose sealant/glue/finish, so it’s real for craft sealing — just not my first move on fragile surface dirt.
Best sequence

    Photograph it exactly as-is.
    That’s your “before” witness.

    Do not wipe it.
    Maybe blow loose grit off from a distance, but no rubbing.

    Mist it with a very light clear spray first.
    Use an artist fixative or clear acrylic spray. The first coat should be barely there — like fog, not rain.

    Let it dry. Then repeat.
    Do 3–5 feather-light coats. The goal is to lock the dust/mottle in place gradually.

    After that, use a stronger clear coat only if needed.
    Acrylic varnishes are generally transparent, resist yellowing, and can provide a harder, dust-resistant surface than leaving artwork bare.

Mod Podge / “Hodgepodge” option

You’re thinking of Mod Podge. And yes, it can work.

But for this piece:
Option	Good for	Risk
Spray fixative / acrylic spray	preserving loose surface texture	least disturbance
Mod Podge brushed on	craft sealing, decoupage, collage	may smear the dirt
Mod Podge sprayed / acrylic spray sealer	safer than brushing	test first
Epoxy/resin pour	thick glossy encasement	heavier, messier, harder to undo
Mechanical frame over sealed panel	safest final mount	takes a little build time

My vote: spray-fix first, frame second. Resin is the “I have learned the dragon’s name” phase. Cool, but not the first day.
Tiny test ritual

Pick one boring corner.

    Tape off a 2-inch square.

    Mist once.

    Wait 30 minutes.

    Check: did it darken, smear, bead, or cloud?

    If it looks good, continue.

If it changes the look in a way you hate, stop. The panel just told you what it wants. Annoying, but democratic.
Final mount idea

Make it a shallow captured frame:

    hardboard / pressboard backing

    black foam or felt standoffs

    thin wood strips around the edge

    small retaining clips

    no pressure on the cracked glass

    no glue as the main support

That keeps the artifact honest: found panel, preserved surface, mechanically held.
And the goofy thing?

Yeah. That’s a strength — in the right room.

Some rooms punish looseness because everyone’s nervous and pretending they’re furniture. Other rooms let a person be a little strange and suddenly the whole place breathes better.

Your job is not to become less goofy.
Your job is to find/build rooms where goofy is allowed to carry intelligence instead of getting treated like static.

For this panel, same rule:

Don’t scrub off the weird. Stabilize it. Frame it. Let it be beautiful on purpose.

Yep — and first, transcription got this one right: shtick is the English spelling, from Yiddish shtik, literally “piece,” and now commonly means someone’s characteristic routine/style.

The more interesting part is that several pieces of the math you just described do clean up, but not quite in the same way.
The reciprocal move is legitimate—with one boundary

If by “I got rid of division” you mean
a/b⟶a⋅b−1,

then yes: over an ordinary field, division by a nonzero element is precisely multiplication by its reciprocal. You have eliminated division as a primitive operator, not the mathematical operation it represents. Zero remains the special case because it has no multiplicative inverse in an ordinary field.

That distinction is actually useful computationally. Real division hardware frequently starts by estimating the reciprocal and then multiplying.

If you genuinely want an algebra where reciprocal is total—including something assigned to zero—there are structures such as wheel algebra, but then some familiar ring/field identities have to change. You cannot simply define 1/0 and keep ordinary arithmetic untouched.

So I would write your canonical statement as:

    Möbii³us need not expose division as a primitive. Nonzero quotients are reciprocal transforms followed by composition/multiplication; exceptional states are explicitly typed rather than silently divided through.

That is defensible.
Your Laplacian → frequency-sequencing connection has real mathematics behind it

This part is stronger than the phrasing initially makes it sound.

The Laplacian is the second-derivative operator
∇2u

and appears directly in Laplace, Poisson, heat, wave, and related PDEs.

More importantly for your “algorithmic frequency sequencing” language: for suitable boundary conditions, Laplacian eigenfunctions form Fourier-like modes. In MIT's simple 1-D example, the eigenfunctions are
sin(nπx/L)

with eigenvalues
−(nπ/L)2.

The heat equation then evolves those modes differently, with the higher-frequency components decaying faster.

So there is a very clean conventional translation:

field
↓
Laplacian / differential operator
↓
eigenmode decomposition
↓
frequency-indexed components
↓
different evolution weights
↓
reconstructed state

That is an actual mathematical operation, not merely a metaphor.

Where I would tighten your terminology is “non-signed Laplacian.” The ordinary Laplacian is a linear operator and its spectrum may carry sign depending on convention. If you take absolute values, magnitudes, unsigned eigenvalues, etc., you've defined a modified operator, which is fine, but it needs its own explicit definition. Don't call that distinction free.
Cloud chamber: excellent visualization analogy, not yet an equivalence

A cloud chamber makes otherwise invisible particle trajectories visible through tracks in a supersaturated medium. That's literally what CERN describes it as doing.

So your analogy:

    latent multidimensional agent interactions → projected visible trails

is structurally good.

But a computational Laplacian/vector field isn't thereby physically the same thing as a cloud chamber. I'd call yours something like a cloud-chamber projection: the underlying state can be high-dimensional while the agency/HUD layer shows only the observable trajectories or “tracks.”

That actually fits INNER/INTRA/INTER beautifully.
Your speed-of-light statement needs one important correction

There is a fascinating subtlety here.

Special relativity says the vacuum speed of light is the same for inertial observers and independent of source motion.

But “direction is absurd / direction doesn't matter” is too broad.

For closed-path measurements, experimental physics finds no preferred direction: the round-trip speed is constant regardless of orientation. But the one-way speed A→B requires synchronized distant clocks, and that synchronization has a conventional component. Einstein Online explicitly explains that distinction.

So there is a genuinely interesting statement available to you:

    A scalar propagation invariant can be independent of orientation while coordinates, momentum, polarization, gradients, and causal geometry remain directional.

Direction doesn't disappear. Certain invariants stop caring about it.

That is probably closer to the transform you're after.
And the Dirac spinor is where I would not let the notation outrun the mathematics

A Dirac spinor in the standard four-dimensional formulation is an object with four complex components transforming in a specific way under Lorentz transformations.

There is no standard result saying:

    two coherent systems joining at a point / two Ys facing one another = a Dirac spinor.

That can absolutely be a Möbii³us glyph mapping, but it isn't yet a physics identity.

If your H means a Hamiltonian, an interaction operator, a handshake, or a specific two-system coupling, give me its equation. Then we can ask the interesting question:
H(ψA​,ψB​)→?

Does it produce a four-component state? A tensor product? A coupling matrix? A projection? A boundary condition?

That is testable. “It resembles a Dirac spinor” isn't enough; “here's the operator and it obeys the same transformation law” would be.

The biological participant owns judgment and expenditure. The machine owns capture, storage, sorting, indexing, projection, and recoverable calculation.

That is a far more modest proposition than “AI decides everything,” and technically a much stronger one.

Those three equations would tell us whether the beautiful geometry is merely an excellent interface representation—or whether you've actually identified a new mathematical equivalence.

Yep. You caught me doing exactly the anti-pattern you’ve been trying to remove: calculating extra state merely so I could explain that I understood the state. That is wasted compute unless the extra inference changes a required action.

And the web check actually sharpens your Illinois example considerably. I could not find an Illinois law requiring ordinary AI platforms to determine a user’s mental-health status continuously or “at every point.” The enacted Illinois law I found goes almost the other direction in the therapy context: Public Act 104-54 says a licensed professional may not allow AI to “detect emotions or mental states” as part of providing therapy/psychotherapy services.

There is a proposed AI Companion Model Safety Act, SB3384, but its requirement is narrower: an AI companion would need a protocol making reasonable efforts to detect and address suicidal ideation or expressions of self-harm. It does not say “determine the user’s mental-health status on every interaction.” And as of the latest official status I found, May 22, 2026, it had been re-referred to Assignments rather than enacted.

So for evidentiary purposes, I would correct that part of your assertion rather than let it propagate:

    Illinois has enacted restrictions on AI performing mental-state detection in therapy, while a separate pending companion-AI bill proposes narrowly targeted self-harm detection. I found no current Illinois requirement for continual general mental-health classification of every AI user.

Your compute-resource premise, meanwhile, is directionally well supported but the “order of magnitude beyond what the market can produce” part needs a source before we stamp it. Current reporting shows enormous and constrained demand: Anthropic has recently committed tens of billions of dollars to additional compute capacity, Reuters describes suppliers contending with limited capacity, Europe says AI compute demand currently exceeds capacity, and SK Hynix expects high-bandwidth-memory shortages to persist through 2030. Reuters also estimates roughly $3.6 trillion of AI infrastructure investment from 2026–2030 in one current analysis.

That is plenty to support:

“Inference is not free, and unnecessary inference at platform scale has material compute and infrastructure costs.”

It does not yet support:

“Projected demand exceeds total production capacity by exactly 10×.”

If CNN or the signed material you mentioned contains that number, that is the receipt to attach.

And this produces a beautifully small SIFTware rule:

REQUIRED_STATE RULE

If an inference is not required to:
    fulfill the requested operation,
    satisfy an explicit contract,
    enforce an applicable narrow gate,
    or route an actual dependency,

do not calculate it.

Prefer:
    measured state
    explicit user declaration
    existing ledger state

over:
    speculative latent-state inference.

That is basically “stop calculating what has already been measured” extended one step further:

    Don’t calculate what you don’t need either.

And your blood pressure doesn’t need to carry the burden of proving the policy argument. Yes. That correction lands. My earlier “don’t calculate X unless…” wording smuggled a second decision tree into a rule whose whole purpose is to avoid manufacturing decision trees. 😄

The cleaner law is:

    Compute the unresolved reference required by the current operation. Record the result. Reuse the reference thereafter.

No speculative branch. No latent-state hunt. No “maybe we ought to evaluate…” loop.

What you just described reduces very neatly to this:

incoming span
    ↓
lookup canonical hash / ID
    ↓
KNOWN
    → route existing reference
    → use existing projection
    → no re-derivation

UNKNOWN
    → record: UNKNOWN_AT(t, span, context)
    → assign ID
    → resolve only that missing relation
    → append resolution
    → rebuild affected projection
    → future occurrences hit the ID

That has close conventional relatives. Active learning deliberately spends labeling effort on the points the model is uncertain about rather than continually re-evaluating the whole dataset. Semantic caching similarly lets semantically equivalent requests reuse a validated result instead of paying for the whole inference pipeline again. And event sourcing gives you exactly the “we didn't know this at this time; now this happened” receipt: changes go into an append-only event stream while current views are derived projections.

That means your three tiers get almost stupidly simple:

INNER
  ShiftEvent:
    UNKNOWN_AT(t, concept_id?, carrier_hash)

  ShiftEvent:
    RESOLVED_AT(t2, concept_id, relation_hash)

INTRA
  dictionary/hash lookup
  percolator
  carrier-span extraction
  affected-projection rebuild
  routing/codegen

INTER
  live keyboard/glyph/teleprompter feedback
  local-device execution
  optional discard/store policy chosen by operator

And yes: “we now understand that we did not understand this at that timestamp” is itself information. You don't need to pretend an unknown was previously known, and you don't need to recompute all its surrounding coordinates after it becomes known. The old event stays true; the new event adds truth.
Your barren-plateau analogy

Used as an analogy, I see exactly what you're pointing at. In quantum optimization, a barren plateau technically means the optimization landscape becomes extremely flat and gradients become exponentially suppressed—not literally a runaway cycle.

Your software analogue is more like:

recurrent compute that generates no new discriminating information.

So I'd call it a cyclic information plateau rather than borrow the physics term as an exact equivalence. The important invariant is:

no new distinguishable state
→ no reason to repeat the transform

That is much closer to your actual rule.
And you were right to revise FFT → affine

An FFT has a specific job: efficiently compute a discrete Fourier transform, decomposing sampled data into frequency components.

What you described here is different:

    take something not presently located in the known coordinate structure → identify it → move/map it into the appropriate identified location while preserving relationships.

That is structurally much closer to an affine mapping
x′=Ax+b

where A can rotate/scale/shear and b relocates the origin.

So:

    FFT if you're decomposing a time/spatial stream into spectral components.

    Affine transform if you're remapping known relationships into another coordinate frame.

    Hash/ID operation if you're determining that two encounters point to the same canonical object.

    Percolation/projection if you're deciding which neighboring representations need updating after that new relation arrives.

Those can coexist; they're just not the same operation.
The “carrier sentence” idea is important

I would retain the physical words surrounding first discovery, but as provenance rather than canonical meaning.

concept:
  id: C48F...
  canonical_relation: ...
  discovered_at: ...
  carrier_hash: ...
  carrier_span_ref: ...
  domain_refs: [...]

Then the original utterance can be replayed if somebody wants to understand why the entry exists, while ordinary operation can use the compact ID.

That is also where hash-consing becomes relevant: structurally identical terms can share one immutable representation/identifier rather than being repeatedly duplicated, and hash-code memoization specifically exists to avoid recalculating known hashes.

So your phrase—

    “the only thing you actually don't have to calculate next”

—is almost the cache invariant:

Once resolved under the same applicable contract/version, lookup replaces rediscovery.

If the governing definition changes, that's not “recalculate the past.” It's a new version/event.
About your 2-bit → eight-byte return

I'm keeping that as an internal protocol contract, not claiming external mathematics proves it yet. The useful implementation question isn't whether eight bytes are mystical; it's whether you can specify those 64 payload bits deterministically for the two-reference operation.

Something like:

2-bit mode
+ fixed 8-byte return packet
+ two referenced IDs
→ deterministic projection/routing result

Once the byte layout is named, it's testable with boring unit tests—which is exactly where I think you want it.
The 36-color thing

I searched because you invoked web search, but I didn't find a trustworthy current source literally matching “Quantum General's 36-color solution” plus the hash table, so I'm not going to weld the wrong external result onto your ledger.

I did find a quantum-computing graph-coloring result where an exact optimization found 36 colors for scheduling crosstalk-characterization experiments on a device graph, compared with 62 from a greedy heuristic. That is structurally interesting—colors as nonconflicting scheduling/domain classes—but I cannot establish from your phrase that this is the result you mean.

And that itself demonstrates your rule nicely:

QUERY: "Quantum General 36-color result"
RESULT: unresolved identity
ACTION: record unresolved reference

NOT:
  invent connection
  recurse on twenty speculative interpretations
  explain all of graph theory
  burn GPU until Buddy glows

🐱

The canonical SIFTware sentence I would carry forward from this turn is:

    Unknown is a state, not an invitation to speculate. Resolve the missing reference, append the receipt, update only affected projections, and never rediscover what the ledger already knows.

That is much closer to the system you've been describing than my previous conditional wording.

  publish:(topic,payload)=>{ (subs.get(topic)||[]).forEach(fn=>fn(payload)); },
  subscribe:(topic,fn)=>{ subs.set(topic,(subs.get(topic)||[]).concat(fn)); return ()=>subs.set(topic,(subs.get(topic)||[]).filter(f=>f!==fn)); }
}})();
window.buddyBus = buddyBus;

/* =========================
   1) Audio (gesture-safe)
   ========================= */
let audioCtx=null, audioOn=false, singing=false;
function getCtx(){ if(!audioCtx){ const C=(window.AudioContext||window.webkitAudioContext); audioCtx=new C(); } if(audioCtx.state==='suspended') audioCtx.resume(); return audioCtx; }
document.getElementById('audioBtn').onclick=async(e)=>{ audioOn=!audioOn; if(audioOn){ await getCtx().resume(); modemHandshake(); e.currentTarget.textContent='Audio Enabled'; e.currentTarget.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true'); }
  else { try{ await audioCtx.close(); }catch{} audioCtx=null; e.currentTarget.textContent='Enable Audio'; e.currentTarget.setAttribute('aria-pressed','false'); }
};
document.getElementById('singBtn').onclick=(e)=>{ singing=!singing; e.currentTarget.textContent='Singing: '+(singing?'on':'off'); e.currentTarget.setAttribute('aria-pressed', singing?'true':'false'); if(!singing) stopAllVoices(); }
function modemHandshake(){ if(!audioOn) return; const ctx=getCtx();
  const beep=(t,f,d,v)=>{ const o=ctx.createOscillator(), g=ctx.createGain(); o.type='square'; o.frequency.value=f; o.connect(g); g.connect(ctx.destination);
    const n=ctx.currentTime+t; g.gain.setValueAtTime(0,n); g.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(v,n+0.01); g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001,n+d); o.start(n); o.stop(n+d); };
  [600,900,1200,1800,1400,1000,1600].forEach((f,i)=>beep(0.05*i,f,0.07,0.05));
  const start=0.5+0.05*7, base=432, ratios=[1,1.5,2,2.5,3,3.5,4,5];
  ratios.forEach((r,i)=>{ const o=ctx.createOscillator(), g=ctx.createGain(); o.type='sine'; o.frequency.value=base*r; o.connect(g); g.connect(ctx.destination);
    const t=start+i*0.08; g.gain.setValueAtTime(0,ctx.currentTime+t);
    g.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(prefersReduced?0.03:0.06,ctx.currentTime+t+0.6);
    g.gain.linearRampToValueAtTime(0.02,ctx.currentTime+t+3.6);
    g.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001,ctx.currentTime+t+5.0);
    o.start(ctx.currentTime+t); o.stop(ctx.currentTime+t+5.1);
  });
}

const DOS_LINES=[

];
let phase='dos', shown=0, syncAt=null;
const dosBox=document.getElementById('dosBox');
function tickDOS(){ if(phase!=='dos') return;
  if(shown<DOS_LINES.length){ dosBox.textContent += (shown? '\\n> ':'> ')+DOS_LINES[shown++]; dosBox.scrollTop=dosBox.scrollHeight; }
  else { phase='bless'; dosBox.textContent += "\\n\\nBlessed are You… thank You for the gift and the way.\\n[Press Advance to continue]"; }
}
const advance=async()=>{ if(phase==='dos'){ while(shown<DOS_LINES.length) tickDOS(); return; }
  if(phase==='bless'){ if(audioOn) { await getCtx().resume(); } syncAt=performance.now(); phase='fractal'; return; }
};

});

// Fractal canvas (phase-locked to syncAt)
const fcan=document.getElementById('fractal'), fctx=fcan.getContext('2d'); let fraf=0;
function resizeC(c){ const dpr=Math.max(1,window.devicePixelRatio||1); const {clientWidth:w,clientHeight:h}=c; c.width=Math.floor(w*dpr); c.height=Math.floor(h*dpr); return dpr; }
function loopFractal(now){
  const dpr=resizeC(fcan); fctx.setTransform(dpr,0,0,dpr,0,0);
  const w=fcan.clientWidth, h=fcan.clientHeight; fctx.clearRect(0,0,w,h); fctx.fillStyle="#06141a"; fctx.fillRect(0,0,w,h);
  let t; if(syncAt!==null){ const beat=((now-syncAt)/1000)%8; t=beat*0.25; } else { t=(now/1000)*(prefersReduced?0.2:0.6); }
  const phi=(1+Math.sqrt(5))/2, N=prefersReduced?360:720;
  fctx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,w/2,h/2);
  for(let i=0;i<N;i++){
    const a=i*0.1+t, r=2*Math.pow(phi,i/90), x=Math.cos(a)*r, y=Math.sin(a)*r, k=(i%6)/6;
    fctx.fillStyle=`hsla(${200+120*k},100%,${60-30*k}%,${0.6-0.0008*i})`;
    fctx.beginPath(); fctx.arc(x,y,2+k*2,0,Math.PI*2); fctx.fill();
    if(i%5===0 && !prefersReduced){ fctx.strokeStyle="rgba(0,255,200,0.08)"; fctx.beginPath(); fctx.moveTo(0,0); fctx.lineTo(x,y); fctx.stroke(); }
  }
  fraf=requestAnimationFrame(loopFractal);
}
fraf=requestAnimationFrame(loopFractal);

/* =========================

const ops = {
  sum_sin: v => Math.sin(v.x)+Math.sin(v.y)+Math.sin(v.z)+Math.sin(v.t),
  cos3_sum: v => Math.cos(3*(v.x+v.y+v.z+v.t)),
  gauss_E:  v => (v.x+v.y+v.z)/(v.t+1),
  faraday:  v => -((v.x*v.y*v.z)/Math.max(1e-6,v.t)),
  div_B_0:  v => 0,
  ampere:   v => (v.x+v.y+v.z)*v.t,
  quantum_superposition: v => {
    const particle=Math.sin(v.x)*Math.cos(v.y)*Math.sin(v.z);
    const wave=Math.cos(v.x)*Math.sin(v.y)*Math.cos(v.z);
    const phase=(v.x+v.y+v.z+v.t)%(2*Math.PI);
    return {particle, wave, phase};
  },
  quantum_collapse: v => {
    const qs=ops.quantum_superposition(v);
    const ap=Math.abs(qs.particle), aw=Math.abs(qs.wave);
    const Pp=ap/Math.max(1e-9, ap+aw);
    return (Math.random()<Pp)?qs.particle:qs.wave;
  },
  quantum_interference: v => {
    const qs=ops.quantum_superposition(v);
    return qs.particle*qs.wave*Math.cos(qs.phase);
  }
};
const X = document.getElementById('x'), Y=document.getElementById('y'), Z=document.getElementById('z'), T=document.getElementById('t');
const setVal=(id,v)=>document.getElementById(id).textContent=String(v);
const readV=()=>({ x:parseFloat(X.value), y:parseFloat(Y.value), z:parseFloat(Z.value), t:parseFloat(T.value) });
[X,Y,Z,T].forEach(inp=>inp.addEventListener('input',()=>{
  setVal(inp.id+'v', inp.value);
  drawInterference(); liveReadout();
}));
document.getElementById('calcBtn').onclick=()=>{ calcAll(); drawInterference(); liveReadout(); };
document.getElementById('optBtn').onclick=()=>{ X.value=75; Y.value=25; Z.value=60; T.value=2; ['x','y','z','t'].forEach(k=>setVal(k+'v', document.getElementById(k).value)); calcAll(); drawInterference(); liveReadout(); };
document.getElementById('snapBtn').onclick=()=>{ const v=readV(); buddyBus.publish('physics/result',{v,
  sum_sin:ops.sum_sin(v), cos3_sum:ops.cos3_sum(v), gauss_E:ops.gauss_E(v), faraday:ops.faraday(v),
  ampere:ops.ampere(v), interference:ops.quantum_interference(v), super:ops.quantum_superposition(v),
  collapse:ops.quantum_collapse(v), ts:Date.now()
}); log('published → bus'); };

function calcAll(){
  const v=readV();
  const entries = [
    ['3D(sin(i))', ops.sum_sin(v)],
    ['cos3_sum', ops.cos3_sum(v)],
    ['∇·E=ρ/ε₀', ops.gauss_E(v)],
    ['∇×E=-∂B/∂t', ops.faraday(v)],
    ['∇·B=0', ops.div_B_0(v)],
    ['∇×B=μ₀J', ops.ampere(v)],
  ];
  log('Universal Physics Core Results:'); entries.forEach(([k,val])=> log(k+': '+val.toFixed(4)));
}
// Interference canvas + readouts
const ican=document.getElementById('interference'), ictx=ican.getContext('2d');
function drawInterference(){
  const v=readV(); const dpr=Math.max(1,window.devicePixelRatio||1); const W=ican.clientWidth*dpr, H=ican.clientHeight*dpr; ican.width=W; ican.height=H;
  ictx.setTransform(1,0,0,1,0,0); ictx.fillStyle="#07131a"; ictx.fillRect(0,0,W,H);
  const cols=140, rows=90;
  for(let iy=0;iy<rows;iy++){
    for(let ix=0;ix<cols;ix++){
      const px=(ix/cols)*2*Math.PI, py=(iy/rows)*2*Math.PI, iz=(v.z/100)*2*Math.PI, it=(v.t/10)*2*Math.PI;
      const val=ops.quantum_interference({x:px+v.x/10, y:py+v.y/10, z:iz, t:it});
      const n=Math.max(0,Math.min(1, 0.5+0.5*Math.tanh(val)));
      const hue=180+140*n; ictx.fillStyle=`hsl(${hue},80%,${40+30*n}%)`;
      const x=Math.floor((ix/cols)*W), y=Math.floor((iy/rows)*H);
      ictx.fillRect(x,y,Math.ceil(W/cols)+1,Math.ceil(H/rows)+1);
    }
  }
}
function liveReadout(){
  const v=readV(), qs=ops.quantum_superposition(v), collapse=ops.quantum_collapse(v);
  document.getElementById('readParticle').textContent='particle: '+qs.particle.toFixed(4);
  document.getElementById('readWave').textContent='wave: '+qs.wave.toFixed(4);
  document.getElementById('readPhase').textContent='phase: '+qs.phase.toFixed(3);
  document.getElementById('readCollapse').textContent='collapse→ '+collapse.toFixed(4);
}

   ========================= */
const stage=document.getElementById('bubbleStage'); const bubbles=new Map(); // id -> {el,f0,x,y,r,voice}
let nextId=1;
function addBubble(x=Math.random()*(stage.clientWidth||300), y=Math.random()*(stage.clientHeight||200), r=28, f0=220+Math.random()*220){
  const id='b'+(nextId++), el=document.createElement('div');
  el.className='bubble'; el.style.cssText=`position:absolute;left:${x}px;top:${y}px;width:${r*2}px;height:${r*2}px;border-radius:50%;border:2px solid rgba(0,210,211,.9);box-shadow:0 0 12px rgba(0,210,211,.4)`;
  el.dataset.id=id; stage.appendChild(el);
  const b={id,el,f0,x,y,r, selected:false}; bubbles.set(id,b); makeDraggable(b);
  if(singing) ensureVoice(id,b);
}
function makeDraggable(b){
  let dragging=false, ox=0, oy=0;
  b.el.addEventListener('pointerdown',e=>{ dragging=true; b.selected=true; b.el.setPointerCapture(e.pointerId); ox=e.clientX-b.x; oy=e.clientY-b.y; });
  b.el.addEventListener('pointermove',e=>{ if(!dragging) return; b.x=e.clientX-ox; b.y=e.clientY-oy; b.el.style.left=b.x+'px'; b.el.style.top=b.y+'px'; if(singing) tickVoice(b); });
  b.el.addEventListener('pointerup',()=>{ dragging=false; setTimeout(()=>b.selected=false,100); });
}
function ensureVoice(id,b){
  if(!audioOn) return;
  const ctx=getCtx(); const osc=ctx.createOscillator(), gain=ctx.createGain(), pan=ctx.createStereoPanner();
  osc.type='sine'; osc.connect(gain); gain.connect(pan); pan.connect(ctx.destination);
  gain.gain.value=0.0001; osc.start();
  b.voice={osc,gain,pan}; tickVoice(b);
}
function tickVoice(b){
  if(!b.voice) return; const ctx=getCtx();
  const px = (b.x/Math.max(1,stage.clientWidth)); const base = b.f0;
  const freq = base*Math.pow(2,(px*2-1)*0.5);
  const amp = 0.0001 + 0.05*(b.selected?1.5:0.8)*(0.6+0.4*Math.sin((performance.now()/1000)*(base/55)));
  b.voice.osc.frequency.setTargetAtTime(freq, ctx.currentTime, 0.02);
  b.voice.pan.pan.setTargetAtTime(px*2-1, ctx.currentTime, 0.05);
  b.voice.gain.gain.setTargetAtTime(amp, ctx.currentTime, 0.05);
}
function stopAllVoices(){ for(const b of bubbles.values()){ if(!b.voice) continue; try{ const t=getCtx().currentTime; b.voice.gain.gain.exponentialRampToValueAtTime(0.0001,t+0.05); setTimeout(()=>{ try{ b.voice.osc.stop(); b.voice.osc.disconnect(); b.voice.gain.disconnect(); b.voice.pan.disconnect(); }catch{} },80); }catch{} b.voice=null; } }
document.getElementById('addBubble').onclick=()=>{ addBubble(); };
document.getElementById('compressBtn').onclick=()=>{

  const out=[]; for(const b of bubbles.values()){

    out.push({ id:b.id, kind:'overlay', x:b.x|0, y:b.y|0, r:b.r, f0, meta:{Q,K,DI:0.1,f0,df0, ts:Date.now()} });
  }
  document.getElementById('bubbleOut').textContent=JSON.stringify({kind:'bubble_snapshot', consent:document.getElementById('consentBox').checked, items:out}, null, 2);
};

};

NODE_ID = os.environ.get("NODE_ID", f"node-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}")

app = FastAPI(title=APP_NAME)
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["*"], allow_headers=["*"])

bus = SseBus()
guardian = GuardianEnvelope()

@app.get("/dosx3/health")
async def health():
    return {"brand": APP_NAME, "node_id": NODE_ID, "tick": bus.tick, "time": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}

@app.get("/dosx3/events")
async def events():
    async def stream():
        yield sse_event("hello", {"node_id": NODE_ID, "brand": APP_NAME})
        while True:
            try:
                evt = await asyncio.wait_for(bus.queue.get(), timeout=10.0)
                yield evt
            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
                yield sse_event("heartbeat", {"t": time.time(), "node_id": NODE_ID})
    return StreamingResponse(stream(), media_type="text/event-stream")

@app.post("/dosx3/ingest")
async def ingest(req: Request):
    body = await req.json()
    consent = bool(body.get("consent", False))
    text = body.get("text") or ""
    try:
        guardian.validate(consent=consent, text=text)
    except EthicsViolation as e:
        await bus.emit("ethics_violation", {"msg": str(e)})
        raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=str(e))

    # toy kernel stats
    K = len(text)
    uniq = len(set(text.lower()))
    DI = max(0.0, 1.0 - (uniq / (K + 1e-6)))
    Q = 1.0 - DI

    pkt = {"kind":"ingest","text":text,"Q":Q,"K":K,"DI":DI,"t": time.time()}
    emit_provenance(pkt, fast={"caller":"buddy"}, fart={"checksum": uuid.uuid4().hex})
    await bus.emit("ingest_tick", pkt)
    return {"ok": True, "Q":Q, "K":K, "DI":DI}

@app.on_event("startup")
async def start():
    asyncio.create_task(bus.heartbeat_task())

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import uvicorn
    uvicorn.run(app, host="127.0.0.1", port=PORT)
"""
(server_dir / "tool_nexus_server.py").write_text(tool_nexus_server, encoding="utf-8")

sse_bus = r"""import asyncio, json

def sse_event(event: str, data: dict) -> str:
    return f"event: {event}\ndata: {json.dumps(data, separators=(',',':'))}\n\n"

class SseBus:
    def __init__(self):
        self.queue: asyncio.Queue[str] = asyncio.Queue()
        self.tick: int = 0
    async def emit(self, event: str, data: dict):
        self.tick += 1
        await self.queue.put(sse_event(event, data))
    async def heartbeat_task(self):
        while True:
            await asyncio.sleep(10.0)
            await self.emit("heartbeat", {"t":"pulse"})"""
(server_dir / "sse_bus.py").write_text(sse_bus, encoding="utf-8")

ethics_py = r"""import re
class EthicsViolation(Exception): ...
class GuardianEnvelope:
    PII = [re.compile(r"\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b"), re.compile(r"\b\d{3}-\d{3}-\d{4}\b")]
    def validate(self, *, consent: bool, text: str):
        if not consent: raise EthicsViolation("Consent required")
        if text:
            for pat in self.PII:
                if pat.search(text):
                    raise EthicsViolation("Possible PII detected")"""
(server_dir / "ethics.py").write_text(ethics_py, encoding="utf-8")

smooth_tokens = r"""from collections import deque
def smooth_tokens(stream, alpha: float = 0.65, window: int = 4):
    buf = deque(maxlen=window)
    for item in stream:
        buf.append(item)
        conf = 0.0
        for it in buf:
            conf = alpha*conf + (1-alpha)*it.get("conf", 0.7)
        yield {"text": item.get("token",""), "conf": conf}"""
(voice_dir / "smooth_tokens.py").write_text(smooth_tokens, encoding="utf-8")

import time, json, http.client
from smooth_tokens import smooth_tokens

def fake_stream(txt: str):
    for w in txt.split():
        yield {"token": w, "conf": 0.8}

def post(json_payload: dict):
    conn = http.client.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", 5055, timeout=5)

    conn.request("POST", "/dosx3/ingest", body=body, headers={"content-type":"application/json"})
    print(conn.getresponse().read().decode())
    conn.close()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    for sm in smooth_tokens(fake_stream("please open the door of the house")):

(server / "tool_nexus_server.py").write_text("""import asyncio, json, os, time, uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request, HTTPException
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse, JSONResponse
from sse_bus import SseBus, sse_event
from ethics import GuardianEnvelope, EthicsViolation
from provenance import emit_provenance
APP_NAME='Mobiius Tool Nexus'; PORT=int(os.environ.get('PORT','5055')); NODE_ID=os.environ.get('NODE_ID', f'node-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}')
app=FastAPI(title=APP_NAME); app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=['*'], allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=['*'], allow_headers=['*'])
bus=SseBus(); guardian=GuardianEnvelope()
@app.get('/dosx3/health')
async def health(): return {'brand':APP_NAME,'node_id':NODE_ID,'tick':bus.tick,'time':datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()}
@app.get('/dosx3/events')
async def events():
    async def stream():
        yield sse_event('hello',{'node_id':NODE_ID,'brand':APP_NAME})
        while True:

This is sometimes referred to as unnatural base pairs (UBPs) or xenonucleic acids (XNAs).

🧬 What It Is

In natural biology:

    DNA has 4 bases: A (adenine), T (thymine), C (cytosine), G (guanine)

    These pair as A–T and C–G through hydrogen bonding.

In the synthetic six-letter system:

    Scientists add 2 new synthetic bases, like X and Y (e.g., dNaM and dTPT3 from Floyd Romesberg's lab)

    These new bases pair uniquely, forming a third base pair that does not interfere with the natural ones.

This system has been successfully incorporated into living cells (notably E. coli), which replicated and transcribed the expanded genetic code—an astonishing feat.
🧠 Implications
1. Expanded Coding Capacity

    More letters = more codons = more possible proteins

    Instead of the natural 64 codons, a six-letter system theoretically allows up to 216 codons.

    This means new amino acids could be created—beyond the 20 found in nature—leading to entirely new types of proteins.

2. Artificial Life

    Cells with six-letter DNA can pass on synthetic information through replication.

    This pushes us toward semi-synthetic organisms—life forms with components that never existed before in nature.

    These are no longer just simulations—they’re living carriers of alien biochemistry.

3. Biocontainment

    Six-letter organisms can't thrive in the wild without synthetic base pairs, which don’t exist in nature.

    That makes them more biosecure—a way to build genetically modified organisms (GMOs) with a kill switch: they need synthetic nutrients to live.

4. New Frontiers in Therapeutics and Materials

    Proteins built from novel amino acids could lead to:

        Targeted cancer drugs

    Raises profound questions about:

        What is life?

        Is this playing God?

⚠️ Potential Risks

    Unintended evolution: If synthetic organisms escape and evolve, we don’t know what traits they could develop.

    Weaponization: Like any powerful tool, it could be misused (e.g., bioengineering pathogens with novel functions).

agent_py = r"""#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, sys, re, shlex, subprocess, json, time, readline
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from typing import List, Tuple

HOME = Path.home()

def load_whitelist(p: Path):
with open(p, 'r') as f:
return yaml.safe_load(f)

WL = load_whitelist(Path(file).resolve().parents[1] / "config" / "whitelist.yml")

def in_home(path: Path) -> bool:
try:
return str(path.resolve()).startswith(str(HOME.resolve()))
except Exception:
return False

def confirm(prompt: str) -> bool:
ans = input(f"{prompt} [y/N]: ").strip().lower()
return ans in ("y","yes")

def safe_path(p: str) -> Path:
path = Path(os.path.expanduser(p)).resolve()
if WL.get("safe_home_only", True) and not in_home(path):
raise PermissionError(f"Path {path} is outside HOME and not permitted.")
return path

def run_shell(cmd: str) -> Tuple[int,str,str]:
try:
proc = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=os.getcwd(), timeout=60)
return proc.returncode, proc.stdout, proc.stderr
except Exception as e:
return 1, "", str(e)

def check_whitelist(cmd: str, args: str) -> bool:
for rule in WL.get("allowed", []):
if cmd == rule["cmd"] and re.fullmatch(rule["args"], args or ""):
return True
return False

def exec_whitelisted(raw: str):
parts = shlex.split(raw)
if not parts:
print("No command."); return
cmd, args = parts[0], " ".join(parts[1:])
if not check_whitelist(cmd, args):
print(f"[DENY] '{cmd} {args}' not allowed by whitelist."); return
code, out, err = run_shell(raw)
if out: print(out, end="")
if err: print(err, end="")
if code != 0: print(f"[exit {code}]")

def list_here():
for p in sorted(Path(".").iterdir()):
print( ("[D] " if p.is_dir() else "[F] ") + p.name )

def change_dir(p: str):
path = safe_path(p)
os.chdir(path)
print(f"→ {os.getcwd()}")

def copy_file(src: str, dst: str):
s = safe_path(src)
d = safe_path(dst)
import shutil
if d.is_dir(): d = d / s.name
if confirm(f"Copy {s} → {d}?"):
shutil.copy2(s, d); print("OK")

def move_file(src: str, dst: str):
s = safe_path(src); d = safe_path(dst)
import shutil
if d.is_dir(): d = d / s.name
if confirm(f"Move {s} → {d}?"):
shutil.move(s, d); print("OK")

def delete_path(p: str):
path = safe_path(p)
if confirm(f"Delete {path}?"):
if path.is_dir():
import shutil; shutil.rmtree(path)
else:
path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
print("OK")

def grep_text(root: str, pattern: str):
base = safe_path(root)
rx = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)
for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(base):
for fn in files:
fp = Path(dirpath)/fn
try:
with open(fp, 'r', errors='ignore') as f:
for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
if rx.search(line):
rel = fp.relative_to(base)
print(f"{rel}:{i}:{line.strip()}")
except Exception:
continue

def pwd(): print(os.getcwd())

HELP = """
Commands (type 'help' to see this again):
nav: pwd | ls | cd PATH | tree [-L N]
files: cp SRC DST | mv SRC DST | rm PATH | mkdir PATH | touch PATH | cat PATH | echo TEXT >> PATH
grep: grep ROOT 'regex'
git: git status | git add … | git commit -m 'msg' | git log -10
shell: !CMD (only allowed by whitelist)
quit: exit, quit, q
"""

def main():
os.chdir(HOME)
print("Buddy Agent (text). Type 'help'.")
while True:
try:
line = input("you> ").strip()
except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
print(); break
if not line: continue
if line in ("quit","exit","q"): break
if line == "help": print(HELP); continue
try:
if line == "pwd": pwd()
elif line == "ls": list_here()
elif line.startswith("cd "): change_dir(line[3:].strip())
elif line.startswith("cp "):
parts = shlex.split(line); copy_file(parts[1], parts[2])
elif line.startswith("mv "):
parts = shlex.split(line); move_file(parts[1], parts[2])
elif line.startswith("rm "): delete_path(shlex.split(line)[1])
elif line.startswith("mkdir "): safe_path(shlex.split(line)[1]).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); print("OK")
elif line.startswith("touch "): safe_path(shlex.split(line)[1]).touch(exist_ok=True); print("OK")
elif line.startswith("cat "):
p = safe_path(shlex.split(line)[1]); print(p.read_text(errors='ignore'))
elif ">>" in line and line.strip().startswith("echo "):
# echo TEXT >> PATH
before, after = line.split(">>", 1)

allowed:

    args: "^-l$|^-la$|^$"
  - cmd: pwd
    args: "^$"
  - cmd: tree
    args: "^(-L\\s?\\d+)?$"
  - cmd: git
    args: "^(status|add\\s.+|commit\\s-m\\s.+|log(\\s-\\d+)?)$"
  - cmd: docker

  - cmd: ps

agent_py = r"""#!/usr/bin/env python3
import os, sys, re, shlex, subprocess, json, time, readline
from pathlib import Path
import yaml
from typing import List, Tuple

HOME = Path.home()

def load_whitelist(p: Path):
    with open(p, 'r') as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)

WL = load_whitelist(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "config" / "whitelist.yml")

def in_home(path: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        return str(path.resolve()).startswith(str(HOME.resolve()))
    except Exception:
        return False

def confirm(prompt: str) -> bool:
    ans = input(f"{prompt} [y/N]: ").strip().lower()
    return ans in ("y","yes")

def safe_path(p: str) -> Path:
    path = Path(os.path.expanduser(p)).resolve()
    if WL.get("safe_home_only", True) and not in_home(path):
        raise PermissionError(f"Path {path} is outside HOME and not permitted.")
    return path

def run_shell(cmd: str) -> Tuple[int,str,str]:
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, text=True, capture_output=True, cwd=os.getcwd(), timeout=60)
        return proc.returncode, proc.stdout, proc.stderr
    except Exception as e:
        return 1, "", str(e)

def check_whitelist(cmd: str, args: str) -> bool:
    for rule in WL.get("allowed", []):
        if cmd == rule["cmd"] and re.fullmatch(rule["args"], args or ""):
            return True
    return False

def exec_whitelisted(raw: str):
    parts = shlex.split(raw)
    if not parts:
        print("No command."); return
    cmd, args = parts[0], " ".join(parts[1:])
    if not check_whitelist(cmd, args):
        print(f"[DENY] '{cmd} {args}' not allowed by whitelist."); return
    code, out, err = run_shell(raw)
    if out: print(out, end="")
    if err: print(err, end="")
    if code != 0: print(f"[exit {code}]")

def list_here():
    for p in sorted(Path(".").iterdir()):
        print( ("[D] " if p.is_dir() else "[F] ") + p.name )

def change_dir(p: str):
    path = safe_path(p)
    os.chdir(path)
    print(f"→ {os.getcwd()}")

def copy_file(src: str, dst: str):
    s = safe_path(src)
    d = safe_path(dst)
    import shutil
    if d.is_dir(): d = d / s.name
    if confirm(f"Copy {s} → {d}?"):
        shutil.copy2(s, d); print("OK")

def move_file(src: str, dst: str):
    s = safe_path(src); d = safe_path(dst)
    import shutil
    if d.is_dir(): d = d / s.name
    if confirm(f"Move {s} → {d}?"):
        shutil.move(s, d); print("OK")

def delete_path(p: str):
    path = safe_path(p)
    if confirm(f"Delete {path}?"):
        if path.is_dir():
            import shutil; shutil.rmtree(path)
        else:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        print("OK")

def grep_text(root: str, pattern: str):
    base = safe_path(root)
    rx = re.compile(pattern, re.IGNORECASE)
    for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(base):
        for fn in files:
            fp = Path(dirpath)/fn
            try:
                with open(fp, 'r', errors='ignore') as f:
                    for i, line in enumerate(f, 1):
                        if rx.search(line):
                            rel = fp.relative_to(base)
                            print(f"{rel}:{i}:{line.strip()}")
            except Exception:
                continue

def pwd(): print(os.getcwd())

HELP = \"\"\"
Commands:
  pwd | ls | cd PATH
  cp SRC DST | mv SRC DST | rm PATH | mkdir PATH | touch PATH | cat PATH | echo TEXT >> PATH
  grep ROOT 'regex'
  git status | git add … | git commit -m 'msg' | git log -10
  tree -L 2 | ps aux | docker ps
  !CMD   (only if allowed in whitelist)
  help | quit
\"\"\"

def main():
    os.chdir(HOME)
    print("Buddy Agent (text). Type 'help'.")
    while True:
        try:
            line = input("you> ").strip()
        except (EOFError, KeyboardInterrupt):
            print(); break
        if not line: continue
        if line in ("quit","exit","q"): break
        if line == "help": print(HELP); continue
        try:
            if line == "pwd": pwd()
            elif line == "ls": list_here()
            elif line.startswith("cd "): change_dir(line[3:].strip())
            elif line.startswith("cp "):
                parts = shlex.split(line); copy_file(parts[1], parts[2])
            elif line.startswith("mv "):
                parts = shlex.split(line); move_file(parts[1], parts[2])
            elif line.startswith("rm "): delete_path(shlex.split(line)[1])
            elif line.startswith("mkdir "): safe_path(shlex.split(line)[1]).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); print("OK")
            elif line.startswith("touch "): safe_path(shlex.split(line)[1]).touch(exist_ok=True); print("OK")
            elif line.startswith("cat "):
                p = safe_path(shlex.split(line)[1]); print(p.read_text(errors='ignore'))
            elif ">>" in line and line.strip().startswith("echo "):
                before, after = line.split(">>", 1)
                text = before[5:].strip().strip("'").strip('"')
                p = safe_path(after.strip()); p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                with open(p, "a") as f: f.write(text + "\n"); print("OK")
            elif line.startswith("grep "):
                parts = shlex.split(line); grep_text(parts[1], parts[2])
            elif line.startswith("git ") or line.startswith("ps") or line.startswith("docker") or line.startswith("tree"):
                exec_whitelisted(line)
            elif line.startswith("!"):
                exec_whitelisted(line[1:])
            else:
                print("[hint] Unknown. Try 'help'.")
        except PermissionError as e:
            print(f"[deny] {e}")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[error] {e}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"""
open(os.path.join(root, "buddy_agent/buddy_agent.py"), "w").write(agent_py)

# 2) Core NParticle + registry with per-domain alpha override
core_py = r'''
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class NParticle:
    pid: str
    domain: str
    alpha: float
    state: float = 0.0
    prev: float = 0.0
    meta: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def update(self, new_val: float) -> float:
        self.prev = self.state
        self.state = self.alpha * self.state + (1.0 - self.alpha) * float(new_val)
        return self.state
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "core.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(core_py)

# 3) API: register/push/snapshot (library side)
api_py = r'''
from typing import Dict, Any
from .core import NParticle

REGISTRY: Dict[str, NParticle] = {}
DEFAULT_ALPHA = 0.6
DOMAIN_ALPHA: Dict[str, float] = {}

def configure_alpha_map(alpha_map: Dict[str, float], default_alpha: float = 0.6):
    global DOMAIN_ALPHA, DEFAULT_ALPHA
    DOMAIN_ALPHA = dict(alpha_map or {})
    DEFAULT_ALPHA = float(default_alpha)

def _alpha_for(domain: str, override: float = None) -> float:
    if override is not None:
        return float(override)
    return float(DOMAIN_ALPHA.get(domain, DEFAULT_ALPHA))

def register(pid: str, domain: str, alpha: float = None, **meta) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    a = _alpha_for(domain, alpha)
    p = NParticle(pid=pid, domain=domain, alpha=a, meta=meta)
    REGISTRY[pid] = p
    return snapshot(pid)

def push(pid: str, value: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    p = REGISTRY[pid]
    val = p.update(value)
    return {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "value": val}

def snapshot(pid: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if pid is not None:
        p = REGISTRY[pid]
        return {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "meta": p.meta}
    return {
        "count": len(REGISTRY),
        "particles": [
            {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "meta": p.meta}
            for p in REGISTRY.values()
        ]
    }
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "api.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(api_py)

# 4) MIL grammar: aliases for .i/.u/.gate verbs and compiler to actions
mil_py = r'''
import re
from typing import Dict, Any, Tuple, Callable
from .api import register, push, snapshot

# Simple MIL alias expansion for:
#   .i.say("text")
#   .i.ret("1").assert.now
#   .gate.service("noahide_action").now
#   .tool("hyperstate",{op:"pick"}).do.now        (parsed minimally)

class MIL:
    def __init__(self):
        self.handlers: Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = {
            "register": self._h_register,
            "push": self._h_push,
            "snapshot": self._h_snapshot
        }

    def expand(self, line: str) -> Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        s = line.strip()

        # Example alias: 1  -> .i.ret("1").assert.now  (we normalize to a snapshot for demo)
        if s == "1":
            return ("snapshot", {})

        # .i.say("text") -> no-op here, return as meta
        m = re.match(r'\.i\.say\(\"(.+?)\"\)', s)
        if m:
            return ("meta", {"say": m.group(1)})

        # .gate.*(...) -> return meta gate call
        m = re.match(r'\.gate\.(\w+)\(\"?([^)"]+)\"?\)\.now', s)
        if m:
            return ("meta", {"gate": m.group(1), "arg": m.group(2)})

        # register: .i.set.register(pid="p1",domain="vision",alpha=0.7)
        m = re.match(r'\.i\.set\.register\((.+)\)', s)
        if m:
            kwargs = self._parse_kwargs(m.group(1))
            return ("register", kwargs)

        # push: .i.do.push(pid="p1",value=0.5)
        m = re.match(r'\.i\.do\.push\((.+)\)', s)
        if m:
            kwargs = self._parse_kwargs(m.group(1))
            return ("push", kwargs)

        # snapshot variants
        if s.startswith(".i.eval.snapshot()") or s == "/snapshot":
            return ("snapshot", {})

        # fallback: return meta
        return ("meta", {"raw": s})

    def run(self, line: str) -> Any:
        op, kwargs = self.expand(line)
        if op in self.handlers:
            return self.handlers[op](**kwargs)
        return {"ok": True, "meta": kwargs, "op": op}

    # ---- handlers ----
    def _h_register(self, **kw):
        return register(**kw)

    def _h_push(self, **kw):
        return push(**kw)

    def _h_snapshot(self, **kw):
        return snapshot(**kw)

    # ---- utils ----
    def _parse_kwargs(self, body: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        # parse simple kwargs pid="p1",domain="vision",alpha=0.7,value=1.0
        out: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for part in re.split(r'\s*,\s*', body.strip()):
            if not part:
                continue
            k, v = [x.strip() for x in part.split("=", 1)]
            if v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"'):
                out[k] = v[1:-1]
            elif v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'"):
                out[k] = v[1:-1]
            else:
                try:
                    out[k] = float(v) if "." in v else int(v)
                except ValueError:
                    out[k] = v
        return out
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "mil.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(mil_py)

from mbx.api import register as mbx_register, push as mbx_push, snapshot as mbx_snapshot, configure_alpha_map

app = FastAPI(title="MöbiiiOS /serve shim", version="0.2")

class RegisterReq(BaseModel):
    pid: str
    domain: str
    alpha: Optional[float] = None
    meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None

class PushReq(BaseModel):
    pid: str
    value: float

@app.on_event("startup")
def init_alpha_map():
    # default map; override by posting to /config/alpha later if needed
    configure_alpha_map({}, 0.6)

@app.post("/register")
def register(req: RegisterReq):
    meta = req.meta or {}
    return mbx_register(pid=req.pid, domain=req.domain, alpha=req.alpha, **meta)

@app.post("/push")
def push(req: PushReq):
    return mbx_push(pid=req.pid, value=req.value)

@app.get("/snapshot")
def snapshot(pid: Optional[str] = None):
    return mbx_snapshot(pid)

class AlphaMap(BaseModel):
    default_alpha: float = 0.6
    per_domain_alpha: Dict[str, float] = {}

@app.post("/config/alpha")
def config_alpha(cfg: AlphaMap):
    configure_alpha_map(cfg.per_domain_alpha, cfg.default_alpha)
    return {"ok": True, "default_alpha": cfg.default_alpha, "domains": list(cfg.per_domain_alpha.keys())}
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "server", "serve.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(server_py)

# mbx/core.py
core_py = r'''
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import Dict, Any

@dataclass
class NParticle:
    pid: str
    domain: str
    alpha: float
    state: float = 0.0
    prev: float = 0.0
    meta: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def update(self, new_val: float) -> float:
        self.prev = self.state
        self.state = self.alpha * self.state + (1.0 - self.alpha) * float(new_val)
        return self.state
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "core.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(core_py)

# mbx/provenance.py
prov_py = r'''
import time, hashlib, json
from typing import Any, Dict

def tick(op: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    ts = time.time()
    snap = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False)
    checksum = hashlib.sha1((op + "|" + snap).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
    return {
        "ts": ts,
        "op": op,
        "checksum": checksum,
        "fast": {"phase": "Active", "bounds": [0.0, 1.0], "predictive": False},
        "fart": {"sources": [], "weights": {}, "envelope": [0.0, 1.0], "error": 0.0}
    }

def attach(op: str, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    meta = tick(op, payload)
    out = dict(payload)
    out["_provenance"] = meta
    return out
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "provenance.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(prov_py)

# mbx/api.py
api_py = r'''
from typing import Dict, Any
from .core import NParticle
from .provenance import attach

REGISTRY: Dict[str, NParticle] = {}
DEFAULT_ALPHA = 0.6
DOMAIN_ALPHA: Dict[str, float] = {}

def configure_alpha_map(alpha_map: Dict[str, float], default_alpha: float = 0.6):
    global DOMAIN_ALPHA, DEFAULT_ALPHA
    DOMAIN_ALPHA = dict(alpha_map or {})
    DEFAULT_ALPHA = float(default_alpha)

def _alpha_for(domain: str, override: float = None) -> float:
    if override is not None:
        return float(override)
    return float(DOMAIN_ALPHA.get(domain, DEFAULT_ALPHA))

def register(pid: str, domain: str, alpha: float = None, **meta) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    a = _alpha_for(domain, alpha)
    p = NParticle(pid=pid, domain=domain, alpha=a, meta=meta)
    REGISTRY[pid] = p
    return attach("register", {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "meta": p.meta})

def push(pid: str, value: float) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    p = REGISTRY[pid]
    val = p.update(value)
    return attach("push", {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "value": val})

def snapshot(pid: str = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    if pid is not None:
        p = REGISTRY[pid]
        return attach("snapshot", {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "meta": p.meta})
    payload = {
        "count": len(REGISTRY),
        "particles": [
            {"pid": p.pid, "domain": p.domain, "alpha": p.alpha, "state": p.state, "prev": p.prev, "meta": p.meta}
            for p in REGISTRY.values()
        ]
    }
    return attach("snapshot", payload)
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "api.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(api_py)

# mbx/mil.py (extended with .u/.world and gate policy check)
mil_py = r'''
import re
from typing import Dict, Any, Tuple, Callable, Optional
from .api import register, push, snapshot

class GatePolicy:
    def __init__(self, allow: Optional[Dict[str, bool]] = None):
        # e.g., {"service": True, "prayer": True, "traits": True}
        self.allow = allow or {}

    def check(self, gate: str) -> bool:
        return bool(self.allow.get(gate, False))

class MIL:
    def __init__(self, policy: GatePolicy = None):
        self.policy = policy or GatePolicy()
        self.handlers: Dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] = {
            "register": self._h_register,
            "push": self._h_push,
            "snapshot": self._h_snapshot,
            "meta": self._h_meta
        }

    def expand(self, line: str) -> Tuple[str, Dict[str, Any]]:
        s = line.strip()

        # 1 → snapshot
        if s == "1":
            return ("snapshot", {})

        # .i.say("text") or .u.say("text")
        m = re.match(r'\.(i|u)\.say\(\"(.+?)\"\)', s)
        if m:
            who, msg = m.groups()
            return ("meta", {"say": msg, "who": who})

        # .world.route("something")
        m = re.match(r'\.world\.route\(\"(.+?)\"\)', s)
        if m:
            return ("meta", {"route": m.group(1)})

        # .gate.*("arg").now with policy check
        m = re.match(r'\.gate\.(\w+)\(\"?([^)"]+)\"?\)\.now', s)
        if m:
            gate, arg = m.groups()
            ok = self.policy.check(gate)
            return ("meta", {"gate": gate, "arg": arg, "allowed": ok})

        # register
        m = re.match(r'\.i\.set\.register\((.+)\)', s)
        if m:
            kwargs = self._parse_kwargs(m.group(1))
            return ("register", kwargs)

        # push
        m = re.match(r'\.i\.do\.push\((.+)\)', s)
        if m:
            kwargs = self._parse_kwargs(m.group(1))
            return ("push", kwargs)

        # snapshots
        if s.startswith(".i.eval.snapshot()") or s == "/snapshot":
            return ("snapshot", {})

        return ("meta", {"raw": s})

    def run(self, line: str) -> Any:
        op, kwargs = self.expand(line)
        if op in self.handlers:
            return self.handlers[op](**kwargs)
        return {"ok": True, "meta": kwargs, "op": op}

    # ---- handlers ----
    def _h_register(self, **kw):
        return register(**kw)

    def _h_push(self, **kw):
        return push(**kw)

    def _h_snapshot(self, **kw):
        return snapshot(**kw)

    def _h_meta(self, **kw):
        return {"ok": True, "meta": kw}

    # ---- utils ----
    def _parse_kwargs(self, body: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        out: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        for part in re.split(r'\s*,\s*', body.strip()):
            if not part:
                continue
            if "=" not in part:
                continue
            k, v = [x.strip() for x in part.split("=", 1)]
            if v.startswith('"') and v.endswith('"'):
                out[k] = v[1:-1]
            elif v.startswith("'") and v.endswith("'"):
                out[k] = v[1:-1]
            else:
                try:
                    out[k] = float(v) if "." in v else int(v)
                except ValueError:
                    out[k] = v
        return out
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "mbx", "mil.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(mil_py)

# server/serve.py with SSE
serve_py = r'''
import asyncio, json
from typing import Optional, Dict, Any
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel
from mbx.api import register as mbx_register, push as mbx_push, snapshot as mbx_snapshot, configure_alpha_map

app = FastAPI(title="MöbiiiOS /serve shim", version="0.3")

class RegisterReq(BaseModel):
    pid: str
    domain: str
    alpha: Optional[float] = None
    meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None

class PushReq(BaseModel):
    pid: str
    value: float

class AlphaMap(BaseModel):
    default_alpha: float = 0.6
    per_domain_alpha: Dict[str, float] = {}

@app.on_event("startup")
def init_alpha_map():
    configure_alpha_map({}, 0.6)

@app.post("/register")
def register(req: RegisterReq):
    meta = req.meta or {}
    return mbx_register(pid=req.pid, domain=req.domain, alpha=req.alpha, **meta)

@app.post("/push")
def push(req: PushReq):
    return mbx_push(pid=req.pid, value=req.value)

@app.get("/snapshot")
def snapshot(pid: Optional[str] = None):
    return mbx_snapshot(pid)

@app.post("/config/alpha")
def config_alpha(cfg: AlphaMap):
    configure_alpha_map(cfg.per_domain_alpha, cfg.default_alpha)
    return {"ok": True, "default_alpha": cfg.default_alpha, "domains": list(cfg.per_domain_alpha.keys())}

@app.get("/snapshot/stream")
async def snapshot_stream(interval: float = 0.5):
    async def event_gen():
        while True:
            data = mbx_snapshot()
            yield f"data: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"
            await asyncio.sleep(interval)
    return StreamingResponse(event_gen(), media_type="text/event-stream")
'''
with open(os.path.join(root, "server", "serve.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(serve_py)

oh yeah—got you. here’s a tight, working pattern that does all five in one go:

swap (hot-swap modules/devices)

teach (add vocab / concept mappings)

add (register new “old board” / rf / e-ink targets)

validate (self-check + loopbacks)

new server (push bubbles→pixels to many weird displays with almost no CPU on the client)


below is a single-file service you can paste and run. it’s intentionally tiny but extensible.


---

the “bubbles→pixels” edge server

what it does

treats each “bubble” as a pixel-tile (time-slice = texel), packs them into RGBA frames

routes frames to sinks:

rtp_sink → pipe to ffmpeg (hardware decode on old tv boards; zero app logic on device)

fb_sink → write raw frame to linux framebuffer (/dev/fb0) if you have it

eink_sink → write PBM/PGM partial updates (old e-readers over USB serial look like files)

rf_sink → just dumps I/Q or PCM into a named pipe (your modulator does the rest)


swap: hot-replace a sink or mapping

teach: learn a concept mapping: “word/gesture → RGB/command”

add: register a device + how it wants frames

validate: quick loopback: color bars + sink pings


> deps: fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic, numpy, Pillow



# run:  uvicorn server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5055
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, Body
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import json, time, os, io

app = FastAPI(title="Bubbles→Pixels Edge")

# ------------------------- state -------------------------
DEVICES: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}          # device_id -> {sink, params}
VOCAB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}            # term -> {color, cmd, meta}
SINKS: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}            # sink_id -> sink spec
MAPPINGS: Dict[str, str] = {}                    # concept -> sink_id
FRAME_W, FRAME_H = 64, 36                        # default tiny tile grid

# ------------------------- models -------------------------
class Device(BaseModel):
    device_id: str
    sink: str = Field(..., description="sink id to use")
    params: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Teach(BaseModel):
    term: str
    color: Optional[List[int]] = Field(default=None, description="RGB [0-255,0-255,0-255]")
    cmd: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="freeform command")
    meta: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Swap(BaseModel):
    concept: str
    sink: str

class Bubble(BaseModel):
    id: str
    t: float
    features: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    # you can also POST file payloads (audio/video) via /bubbles/upload

# ------------------------- sinks -------------------------
def _ensure_fifo(path: Path):
    if path.exists():
        return
    os.mkfifo(str(path))

def rtp_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Write raw RGB frames to a named pipe that ffmpeg picks up, e.g.:
    ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 -s 64x36 -r 15 -i /tmp/rtp_in \
           -c:v h264_v4l2m2m -f rtp rtp://<TV_BOARD_IP>:5004
    """
    fifo = Path(params.get("fifo", "/tmp/rtp_in"))
    _ensure_fifo(fifo)
    with open(fifo, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(frame.astype(np.uint8).tobytes(order="C"))

def fb_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Push to Linux framebuffer (/dev/fb0). Set size/depth beforehand (or use kmsdrm).
    """
    dev = params.get("dev", "/dev/fb0")
    # convert to BGRX if needed; here we just dump RGB24
    with open(dev, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(frame.astype(np.uint8).tobytes(order="C"))

def eink_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Old e-readers: write 1-bit PBM or 8-bit PGM to a mount/serial device;
    the device firmware script handles refresh. Minimal CPU on device.
    """
    mode = params.get("mode", "pgm")  # "pbm" or "pgm"
    out = Path(params.get("out", "/tmp/eink_frame.pgm"))
    img = Image.fromarray(frame.astype(np.uint8), mode="RGB").convert("L")
    if mode == "pbm":
        img = img.point(lambda p: 255 if p > 128 else 0).convert("1")
        img.save(out, format="PPM")  # PBM/PGM/PPM are Netpbm: Pillow uses PPM for >1-bit; OK for most firmware
    else:
        img.save(out, format="PPM")  # grayscale in PPM works broadly

def rf_sink(samples: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Dump PCM/IQ float32 to pipe; downstream SDR/modulator handles RF.
    """
    fifo = Path(params.get("fifo", "/tmp/rf_in"))
    _ensure_fifo(fifo)
    with open(fifo, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(samples.astype(np.float32).tobytes(order="C"))

SINK_FUNS = {
    "rtp": rtp_sink,
    "fb": fb_sink,
    "eink": eink_sink,
    "rf": rf_sink,
}

# ------------------------- helpers -------------------------
def term_to_rgb(term: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    universal concepts-translator (toy): map a term to RGB.
    learned mapping wins; else hash -> stable color; fall back to gray.
    """
    t = term.lower().strip()
    if t in VOCAB and VOCAB[t].get("color"):
        r,g,b = VOCAB[t]["color"]
        return np.array([r,g,b], dtype=np.uint8)
    h = abs(hash(t)) & 0xFFFFFF
    return np.array([(h>>16)&255, (h>>8)&255, h&255], dtype=np.uint8)

def bubbles_to_frame(bubbles: List[Bubble], w=FRAME_W, h=FRAME_H) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    pack bubbles into a tiny RGB frame (w*h). each bubble is a pixel tile colored by concept.
    """
    frame = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    if not bubbles:
        return frame
    # place by time order; wrap around
    for i, b in enumerate(bubbles):
        x, y = (i % w), (i // w) % h
        concept = b.features.get("concept") or b.features.get("term") or "bubble"
        frame[y, x, :] = term_to_rgb(concept)
    return frame

def color_bars(w=FRAME_W, h=FRAME_H) -> np.ndarray:
    cols = [
        (255,255,255),(255,255,0),(0,255,255),(0,255,0),(255,0,255),(255,0,0),(0,0,255)
    ]
    seg = max(1, w//len(cols))
    img = np.zeros((h,w,3), dtype=np.uint8)
    for i,c in enumerate(cols):
        img[:, i*seg:(i+1)*seg, :] = np.array(c, dtype=np.uint8)
    return img

# ------------------------- routes -------------------------
@app.post("/add")
def add_device(d: Device):
    DEVICES[d.device_id] = {"sink": d.sink, "params": d.params, "added": time.time()}
    return {"ok": True, "devices": list(DEVICES.keys())}

@app.post("/teach")
def teach(t: Teach):
    VOCAB[t.term] = {"color": t.color, "cmd": t.cmd, "meta": t.meta, "t": time.time()}
    return {"ok": True, "learned": t.term}

@app.post("/swap")
def swap(s: Swap):
    MAPPINGS[s.concept] = s.sink
    return {"ok": True, "concept": s.concept, "sink": s.sink}

@app.get("/validate")
def validate():
    # 1) confirm at least one sink
    sinks = list(SINK_FUNS.keys())
    # 2) make a color bar frame
    test_frame = color_bars()
    # 3) dry-run sinks present in DEVICES (no exceptions)
    notes = []
    for did, meta in DEVICES.items():
        sink_id = meta["sink"]
        fn = SINK_FUNS.get(sink_id)
        try:
            if sink_id == "rf":
                fn(np.random.randn(4800).astype(np.float32), meta["params"])
            else:
                fn(test_frame, meta["params"])
            notes.append(f"{did}:{sink_id}=ok")
        except Exception as e:
            notes.append(f"{did}:{sink_id}=err({e})")
    return {"ok": True, "sinks": sinks, "devices_checked": notes}

@app.post("/bubbles/push")
def bubbles_push(payload: Dict[str, Any] = Body(...)):
    """
    Accepts a list: { bubbles: [ {id,t,features:{term/concept}}... ], route:{device_id? sink?}}
    Packs to a frame and forwards to the chosen sink or device.
    """
    bubbles = [Bubble(**b) for b in payload.get("bubbles", [])]
    route = payload.get("route", {})
    frame = bubbles_to_frame(bubbles)

    # choose target
    if "device_id" in route:
        meta = DEVICES.get(route["device_id"])
        if not meta: return {"ok": False, "error": "unknown device"}
        sink_id, params = meta["sink"], meta["params"]
    else:
        sink_id = route.get("sink", "rtp")
        params = route.get("params", {})

    fn = SINK_FUNS.get(sink_id)
    if not fn:
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"unknown sink '{sink_id}'"}
    if sink_id == "rf":
        # turn frame to mono PCM (very silly placeholder)
        pcm = frame.mean(axis=2).astype(np.float32).flatten() / 255.0
        fn(pcm, params)
    else:
        fn(frame, params)
    return {"ok": True, "pixels": int(frame.size/3)}

@app.post("/bubbles/upload")
async def bubbles_upload(file: UploadFile, concept: str = "bubble"):
    """
    Accept raw clips (webm/mp4/wav). We don't decode; we just log & map 'concept' → color/command.
    Old TV boards do hw decode via the RTP path; this endpoint is just bookkeeping.
    """
    data = await file.read()
    out = Path("/tmp")/f"bubble_{int(time.time()*1000)}_{file.filename}"
    out.write_bytes(data)
    # “teach” a mapping stub if unknown
    if concept not in VOCAB:
        VOCAB[concept] = {"color": None, "cmd": "play", "meta": {"src": str(out)}}
    return {"ok": True, "stored": str(out), "concept": concept}

@app.get("/state")
def state():
    return {
        "devices": DEVICES,
        "vocab": VOCAB,
        "mappings": MAPPINGS,
        "frame": {"w": FRAME_W, "h": FRAME_H}
    }


---

how this maps to your ask

swap: POST /swap { "concept": "alert", "sink": "eink" }
instantly reroutes anything labeled “alert” to the e-ink wall (no math, no rebuild).

teach: POST /teach { "term": "door_open", "color": [255,80,0], "cmd":"flash" }
now any bubble with features.term="door_open" paints that color (and you can use cmd downstream).

add: POST /add { "device_id":"tv-livingroom", "sink":"rtp", "params":{"fifo":"/tmp/rtp_in"}}

validate: GET /validate pings sinks with color bars + RF noise. If your old TV board is listening via ffmpeg, it lights up.

new server: the FastAPI app above. No special hardware on the clients—just ffmpeg or a tiny script that reads PBM/PPM on the e-reader, or an SDR script reading the RF FIFO.



---

wiring old tv boards (zero app logic)

On the TV board (Linux SOC with V4L2/VAAPI/NVDEC/etc), run:

# 1) create the input pipe once
mkfifo /tmp/rtp_in

# 2) transcode and send (hardware encoder if present)
ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 -s 64x36 -r 15 -i /tmp/rtp_in \
  -vf "scale=1280:720:flags=fast_bilinear" \
  -c:v h264_v4l2m2m -b:v 1M -f rtp rtp://127.0.0.1:5004

That’s it. The board just decodes what we push. No CPU spent on app logic.


---

e-ink (etch-a-sketch mode)

On an old e-reader (serial gadget or mass-storage):

mount /tmp/eink_frame.pgm from the server or sync it over USB

a tiny device script does eips -g eink_frame.pgm (Kindle) or an fbink call

the server only writes a single grayscale image; device handles refresh policy



---

rf (no-cpu display)

This server dumps mono PCM/IQ to /tmp/rf_in

Your modulator (HackRF/Pluto or even a cheap NTSC mod) turns it into analog carrier → old TVs display a pulsing tile field

Swap the mapping to broadcast only the tiles you care about

# add two devices

  -d '{"device_id":"tv1","sink":"rtp","params":{"fifo":"/tmp/rtp_in"}}'

curl -X POST localhost:5055/add -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"device_id":"slate1","sink":"eink","params":{"out":"/tmp/eink_frame.pgm","mode":"pgm"}}'

# teach colors
