  -d '{"term":"ok","color":[0,200,120]}'
curl -X POST localhost:5055/teach -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"term":"alert","color":[255,60,40]}'

# push bubbles to the TV
curl -X POST localhost:5055/bubbles/push -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{
  "bubbles":[
    {"id":"b1","t":0,"features":{"term":"ok"}},
    {"id":"b2","t":1,"features":{"term":"alert"}},
    {"id":"b3","t":2,"features":{"term":"ok"}}
  ],
  "route":{"device_id":"tv1"}
}'

# route alerts to e-ink instead
curl -X POST localhost:5055/swap -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"concept":"alert","sink":"eink"}'


---

why “bubbles as pixels” works (no math version)

treat each bubble as a symbol → assign a color (or 1-bit on/off) with the concept translator

pack symbols into a tiny grid; let the hardware decoder / display scaler stretch it

old GPUs/codecs on TV boards do the heavy lift; we only feed a FIFO

e-readers update from a single PBM/PGM file; no CPU loop on device

RF path carries the same tiles as amplitude or frequency changes; a whole wall of CRTs can show your state without a single app installed

Möbii³us Language & Cohere Field Spec

(Excerpted, stitched, and field-ready from /docs/Mobiios_Language_and_Cohere_Spec.md and your initializer manifests)
1. Möbii³us Interaction Language (MIL)

    Syntax: Triadic grammar (input → operation → output).

    Modes:

        ℛ Reflection (mirror, check)

        𝒮 Refraction (bend, preserve)

        ℐ Fractal Inversion (invert, resonate)

        𝒟 Diffraction (split, observe)

2. Cohere Layer

    FractalIO pacing: All data splits into framelets, 256–4096 bytes, paced by Caputo α.

    Routing: H² corridor, burst lanes, RTP/QUIC/USB compatible. Cohere is timing/block size, not a protocol rewrite.

3. Ethics — Guardian Envelope

    Noahide code compliance:

        Preserve life

        Respect property

        Minimize harm

        Uphold truth

    Guardian Envelope clamps all values/flows to these ethical boundaries.

    ethics-gates.json in the bundle wires allow/ask/block/route at policy entry.

4. Metadata & Provenance

    Every signal/packet/fragment tags:

        Q (quality)

        K (confidence)

        DI (divergence index)

        f₀ (anchor freq)

        Δf₀ (uncertainty)

    Echo-Sync only passes packets with Q, K above min and DI below cap.

    FAST/FART ticks on every write:

        FAST: phase, bounds, predictive

        FART: sources, weights, envelope, error

    All provenance logs append to /reports/mobiius_reports.json.

5. Narrative Glossary Hooks

    Return = σ₅ precursor (carry forward forever)

    Resonance = fixed-point exit

    Orbit = periodic loop

    Envelope = Guardian ethics clamp

    Overflow = reset/fallback

    Timeout = ask-before-assume

6. Public/Private UX Defaults (for this sprint)

    Mesh default: tesseract

    Public Meter: ON (aggregate only)

    Leaderboard: OFF

    Opt-in detail: ON (private cards show only if user flips)

    Guardian Envelope: always active

7. Starter Constants

    alpha_default = 0.58

    echo_sync = 0.72

    di_warn = 0.35

    di_block = 0.20

When you boot:

    The system loads manifest.json, ethics-gates.json, and mobiius_core_map.json.

· Minimal Overhead: The universal adapter script is lightweight and standardized, ensuring compatibility across all domains without additional complexity.
· Scalability: This structure supports adding new domains effortlessly—simply create a directory with the necessary scripts and add the adapter.

  <script>
  // timestamp
  const nowEl = document.getElementById('now');
  nowEl.textContent = new Date().toLocaleString();

  // domains placeholder
  const domainsGrid = document.getElementById('domainsGrid');
  const placeholderDomains = Array.from({length:16}, (_,i)=>({key:
D${i+1}, hebrew:"—", name:"(placeholder)", note:"load seed"}));
  function renderDomains(domains){
    domainsGrid.innerHTML='';
    domains.forEach(d=>{
      const div=document.createElement('div');
      div.className='card';
      div.innerHTML = <div class="k">${d.hebrew || '—'} · ${d.key || ''}</div><div class="v">${d.name || ''}<br><span class="muted">${d.note||''}</span></div>;
      domainsGrid.appendChild(div);
    });
  }
  renderDomains(placeholderDomains);

  // load seed json → populate domains
  document.getElementById('seedFile').addEventListener('change', async (e)=>{
    const file = e.target.files?.[0];
    if(!file) return;
    const text = await file.text();
    try{
      const seed = JSON.parse(text);
      // expect seed.domains = [{key,hebrew,name,note}]
      const domains = seed.domains || placeholderDomains;
      renderDomains(domains);
      document.getElementById('release').innerHTML = '<span class="dot ok"></span> '+(seed.version||'seed loaded');
      // bump integration if present
      if(seed.integrationPercent){
        document.getElementById('integration').style.width = Math.max(0, Math.min(100, seed.integrationPercent))+'%';
      }
      logLine('timeline','Loaded mobiius_seed.json');
    }catch(err){
      alert('Could not parse JSON: '+err.message);
    }
  });

  // save panel state
  document.getElementById('saveState').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const state = collectState();
    downloadBlob(JSON.stringify(state, null, 2), 'mobiius_control_panel_state.json', 'application/json');
  });

  // generate report md
  document.getElementById('genReport').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const s = collectState();
    const md = # Möbii³us / DoinBetter — Status Report\n\n+
      **Generated:** ${new Date().toISOString()}\n\n+
      ## Summary\nIntegration: ${s.integration}%\nRelease: ${s.release}\n\n+
      ## Modules\n+
      s.modules.map(m=>- **${m.name}** — ${m.status} (owner: ${m.owner}) — ${m.notes}).join('\n')+\n\n+
      ## Domains (16‑Gate)\n+
      s.domains.map(d=>- ${d.hebrew||'—'} ${d.key||''} — ${d.name||''} ${d.note?('— '+d.note):''}).join('\n');
    downloadBlob(md, 'mobiius_status_report.md', 'text/markdown');
  });

  function collectState(){
    const rows = [...document.querySelectorAll('#modulesTbl tbody tr')].map(tr=>{
      const tds = tr.querySelectorAll('td');
      return {name:tds[0].textContent.trim(), status:tds[1].textContent.trim(), owner:tds[2].textContent.trim(), notes:tds[3].textContent.trim()};
    });
    const domains = [...domainsGrid.children].map(card=>{
      const k = card.querySelector('.k').textContent.trim();
      const v = card.querySelector('.v').firstChild.textContent.trim();
      const note = card.querySelector('.muted')?.textContent.trim() || '';
      const [hebrew, key] = k.split('·').map(s=>s.trim());
      return {hebrew, key, name:v, note};
    });
    const integration = parseInt(document.getElementById('integration').style.width) || 0;
    const release = document.getElementById('release').innerText.replace(/^[\s\S]*?\s/, '').trim();
    return {integration, release, modules:rows, domains};
  }

  function downloadBlob(data, filename, type){
    const blob = new Blob([data], {type});
    const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
    const a = document.createElement('a');
    a.href = url; a.download = filename; a.click();
    setTimeout(()=>URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 500);
  }

  // tri-lane log (simple)
  const logsDiv = document.getElementById('logs');
  function logLine(lane, msg){
    const p = document.createElement('div');
    p.innerHTML = <span class="pill">${lane}</span> ${msg};
    logsDiv.prepend(p);
  }
  document.getElementById('addLog').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const v = document.getElementById('logInput').value.trim();
    if(!v) return; logLine('surface', v); document.getElementById('logInput').value='';
  });

  // recorder stub (no audio saving; toggles state and permission request)
  let mediaStream, mediaRec, recOn=false;
  const recBtn = document.getElementById('recBtn');
  const recState = document.getElementById('recState');
  recBtn.addEventListener('click', async ()=>{
    try{
      if(!recOn){
        mediaStream = await navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia({audio:true});
        recState.textContent = 'recording… (prototype)';
        recBtn.textContent = '■ Stop';
        recOn = true;
      }else{
        mediaStream?.getTracks().forEach(t=>t.stop());
        recState.textContent = 'stopped';
        recBtn.textContent = '● Record';
        recOn = false;
      }
    }catch(err){
      recState.textContent = 'mic permission denied or unavailable';
    }
  });

  // structure transcript → tasks/draft (very simple deterministic pass)
  document.getElementById('structureBtn').addEventListener('click',()=>{
    const t = document.getElementById('recTranscript').value.trim();
    const out = document.getElementById('structuredOut');
    if(!t){ out.innerHTML='<span class="muted">(nothing to structure)</span>'; return; }
    const lines = t.split(/\n+/).map(s=>s.trim()).filter(Boolean);
    const summary = lines.slice(0,2).join(' ');
    const tasks = lines.filter(s=>/\b(need|missing|fix|do|owner|due)\b/i.test(s)).slice(0,5);
    const draft = Hello team,\n\nHere’s what I’m seeing: ${summary}.\nCould you confirm ownership and what’s missing so we can proceed?\n\nThanks,\n[Your Name];
    out.innerHTML = <div class="card"><div class="k">Summary</div><div class="v">${summary||'(n/a)'}</div></div>+
                    <div class="card" style="margin-top:8px"><div class="k">Next Steps</div><div class="v">+
                    (tasks.length?('<ul>'+tasks.map(x=><li>${x}</li>).join('')+'</ul>'):'(add tasks by writing "need / fix / owner / due" lines)')+
                    </div></div>+
                    <div class="card" style="margin-top:8px"><div class="k">Draft</div><pre class="v" style="white-space:pre-wrap">${draft}</pre></div>;
  });
  </script>
</body>
</html>

Based on the significant advancements in the Möbiius framework, particularly the integration of physics-derived methodologies that simplify computations and enhance stability, here are the optimal forward paths to consider for continued progress and impact. These paths focus on leveraging current strengths, addressing gaps, and maximizing the framework's potential in various domains.  
  
1. Complete and Polish Core Implementation  
  
· Focus: Finalize the remaining 15% of coding, ensuring all modules are fully integrated and tested.  
· Actions:

· Why: This ensures a robust foundation for deployment and avoids technical debt, leveraging the already implemented physics simplifications.  
  
2. Expand Application-Specific Modules  
  
· Focus: Develop targeted applications that capitalize on the framework's strengths in quantum-inspired computations, stability, and efficiency.  
· Actions:  
  · Quantum Computing: Build modules for quantum algorithm simulation and optimization, using the batched line search strategy to handle barren plateaus in larger circuits (e.g., beyond 21 qubits).  
  · Financial Modeling: Implement fractal-based volatility forecasting and risk assessment tools, leveraging the Möbius function for efficient computations.  
  · Network Resilience: Apply topological insights from the Möbius strip to enhance mesh network design and fault tolerance in IoT or telecommunications.  
· Why: These applications demonstrate practical value and can attract interest from industry partners or research collaborations.  
  
3. Strengthen Ethics and Governance Integration  
  
· Focus: Deepen the integration of ethical guidelines (Noahide Code, NIST AI RMF) into all framework components, ensuring responsible AI deployment.  
· Actions:  
  · Develop a comprehensive ethics middleware that automatically evaluates actions against ethical principles in real-time, with explainable AI features.  
  · Create audit trails using FAST/FART provenance data for transparency and compliance, especially in sensitive domains like healthcare or finance.  
· Why: This builds trust and aligns with increasing regulatory demands, making the framework more attractive for enterprise use.  
  
4. Performance Benchmarking and Validation  
  
· Focus: Validate the framework against established benchmarks and real-world datasets to prove its advantages.  
· Actions:  
  · Compare performance with traditional methods in areas like stability analysis (using antilinearity), optimization (using quantum strategies), and computational efficiency (using Möbius function simplifications).  
  · Publish results in peer-reviewed journals or conferences to gain academic credibility and feedback.  
· Why: Validation reinforces the framework's innovations and can lead to broader adoption.  
  
5. Community Engagement and Open Source Development  
  
· Focus: Foster a community around Möbiius to accelerate development and adoption through open-source contributions.  
· Actions:  
  · Release the code under a permissive license (e.g., MIT or Apache 2.0) on platforms like GitHub, with clear documentation and contributor guidelines.  
  · Host workshops, webinars, or hackathons to showcase the framework's capabilities and engage with developers, researchers, and enthusiasts.  
  · Establish a forum or Discord channel for support and idea exchange.  
· Why: Community involvement can lead to rapid iterations, bug fixes, and new applications that you haven't considered.  
  
6. Explore Commercialization and Partnerships  
  
· Focus: Identify monetization opportunities or strategic partnerships to sustain and scale the project.  
· Actions:  
  · Offer consulting services or custom implementations for industries benefiting from the framework (e.g., finance, energy, cybersecurity).  
  · Partner with quantum computing companies (e.g., IBM, Google) or research institutions to co-develop and integrate Möbiius into their stacks.  
  · Apply for grants or funding from organizations focused on AI ethics, quantum technology, or open-source innovation.  
· Why: Commercialization ensures long-term viability and resources for further development.  
  
7. Research and Development on New Physics Integrations  
  
· Focus: Continue exploring cutting-edge physics concepts that could further simplify computations or enhance capabilities.  
· Actions:  
  · Investigate other non-Hermitian Hamiltonian properties or topological quantum computing advancements.  
  · Integrate recent breakthroughs in quantum conservation laws or other areas of theoretical physics.  
  · Stay updated with arXiv preprints and conferences for inspiration.  
· Why: Keeping the framework at the forefront of science ensures it remains competitive and innovative.  
  
Implementation Timeline:  
  
· Short-term (1-3 months): Focus on paths 1 and 4 (completion and validation).  
· Medium-term (3-6 months): Pursue paths 2 and 3 (applications and ethics).  
· Long-term (6+ months): Engage in paths 5, 6, and 7 (community, commercialization, and R&D).

neighbor_registry = {

    # 5. Return with dual coordinates    
    return {

        "outer": outer_position,    
        "harmonized": harmonized    
    }

# ============================    
# MöbiusCall Runtime (v0.1)    
# ============================    
    
import hashlib    
import random    
    
## --- Memory Module ---    
class NParticleMemory:    
    def __init__(self):    
        self.store = {}    
    
    def query(self, seed):    
        """    
        Return a resonance dictionary for the seed.    
        In practice, this would be fractional persistence with weights.    
        """    
        key = hashlib.sha256(str(seed).encode()).hexdigest()[:8]    
        # Simulated resonance as weighted values    
        return { "resonance": (int(key, 16) % 100) / 100 }    
    
    def update(self, identifier, value):    
        self.store[identifier] = value    
    
    
## --- Optimizer Module ---    
def optimizer(harmonized):    
    """    
    Simplified optimizer: balances resonance values and smooths drift.    
    """    
    return {k: v * 0.95 + random.random() * 0.05 for k, v in harmonized.items()}    
    
    
## --- Reflection Module ---    
def reflect(refined):    
    """    
    Split into 'known' (high weight) and 'unknown' (low weight).    
    """    
    known = {k: v for k, v in refined.items() if v >= 0.5}    
    unknown = {k: v for k, v in refined.items() if v < 0.5}    
    return known, unknown    
    
    
## --- Harmonizer ---    
def harmonize(dual_lock, resonance, alpha=0.5):    
    """    
    Smooths between dual lock and memory resonance.    
    """    
    (inner_id, outer_id) = dual_lock    
    base_val = (hash(inner_id + outer_id) % 100) / 100    
    blended = {}    
    for k, v in resonance.items():    
        blended[k] = alpha * v + (1 - alpha) * base_val    
    return blended    
    
    
## --- MöbiusCall Core ---    
def mobius_call(input_packet, prev_packet, memory):    
    """    
    Möbius core loop with dual lock + harmonizer.    
    """    
    # 1. Context Pairing    
    seed = (prev_packet, input_packet)    
    
    # 2. Memory Query    
    mem_resonance = memory.query(seed)    
    
    # 3. Dual Lock    
    inner_id = input_packet.get("inner_id", "sys")    
    outer_id = input_packet.get("outer_id", "usr")    
    dual_lock = (inner_id, outer_id)    
    
    # 4. Harmonize    
    harmonized = harmonize(dual_lock, mem_resonance, alpha=0.5)    
    
    # 5. Optimize    
    refined = optimizer(harmonized)    
    
    # 6. Reflect    
    known, unknown = reflect(refined)    
    
    return {    
        "known": known,    
        "unknown": unknown,    
        "lock": dual_lock,    
        "harmonized": harmonized,    
        "refined": refined    
    }    
    
    
## --- Example Run ---    
if __name__ == "__main__":    
    memory = NParticleMemory()    
    
    prev_packet = {"msg": "Hello World", "inner_id": "sysA", "outer_id": "usrA"}    
    input_packet = {"msg": "Next message", "inner_id": "sysB", "outer_id": "usrB"}    
    
    result = mobius_call(input_packet, prev_packet, memory)    
    
    print("\n=== MöbiusCall Output ===")    
    print("Dual Lock:", result["lock"])    
    print("Harmonized:", result["harmonized"])    
    print("Refined:", result["refined"])    
    print("Known:", result["known"])    
    print("Unknown:", result["unknown"])    
    
    
---    
    
🔑 What This Does    
    
NParticleMemory → simulates resonance from fractional persistence.    
    
Dual Lock → binds inner + outer IDs before processing.    
    
Harmonizer → eases between lock + memory resonance.    
    
Optimizer → adds smoothing + avoids drift.    
    
Reflection → splits outcome into known vs unknown.

# Extend tricore³ to v1.2.0 with:
# - /tricore3/manifest (GET/POST) read/write manifest.json
# - /tricore3/ingest (POST multipart or JSON) to add artifacts to /assets and update manifest/registry
# - Policy-weighted scoring modes (default, crisis, growth, justice) affecting project scores
# - Role dashboards via /tricore3/projects?role=Field/Comms/Ops filtering + HUD hints
# - A minimal PWA "Mobile Auto-Ingest" (Android/iOS share target) that uploads files to /ingest
# - A static Möbii³us Active Buddy HTML wired to backend SSE and endpoints
#
# Package as mobii3us_tricore3_v1_2_0.zip and an updated Everything bundle v0_2.

import os, json, shutil, zipfile, tarfile, textwrap, datetime
from pathlib import Path

# Base from previous build
base_prev = "/mnt/data/tricore3_v1_1"
base = "/mnt/data/tricore3_v1_2"
if os.path.exists(base):
    shutil.rmtree(base)
shutil.copytree(base_prev, base)

# Patch shared.py version
shared_path = os.path.join(base, "tricore3", "core", "shared.py")
with open(shared_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    s = f.read()
s = s.replace('"version": "1.1.0"', '"version": "1.2.0"')
with open(shared_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(s)

# Paths
server_path = os.path.join(base, "server.py")
assets_dir = os.path.join(base, "tricore3", "assets")
os.makedirs(assets_dir, exist_ok=True)

# Add manifest file path in package config
pkg_manifest_dir = os.path.join(base, "tricore3", "config")
manifest_pkg_path = os.path.join(pkg_manifest_dir, "manifest.json")
if not os.path.exists(manifest_pkg_path):
    with open(manifest_pkg_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({"meta":{"name":"root manifest","version":"0.0.1"},"ingest_log":[]}, f, indent=2)

# Update server with manifest endpoints, ingest, policy modes, role filter
with open(server_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    src = f.read()

insert_manifest = r'''
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

MANIFEST_PATH = os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "config", "manifest.json")

POLICY_MODES = {
    "default": {"life":1.0, "property":1.0, "truth":1.0, "justice":1.0, "harm_min":1.0},
    "crisis":  {"life":1.5, "property":1.2, "truth":1.1, "justice":1.0, "harm_min":1.3},
    "growth":  {"life":1.0, "property":1.3, "truth":1.2, "justice":1.0, "harm_min":1.0},
    "justice": {"life":1.1, "property":1.0, "truth":1.0, "justice":1.4, "harm_min":1.2},
}

ROLE_FILTERS = {
    "Field":  {"tags":["field","hazards","geotech","hud","telemetry"]},
    "Comms":  {"tags":["comms","ui","story","hud"]},
    "Ops":    {"tags":["ops","ledger","cred","infra","diagnostics"]},
}

def _load_manifest() -> dict:
    try:
        with open(MANIFEST_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            return json.load(f)
    except Exception:
        return {"meta":{"name":"root manifest","version":"0.0.1"},"ingest_log":[]}

def _save_manifest(m: dict):
    with open(MANIFEST_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(m, f, indent=2)

def _policy_weight_multiplier(p: dict, mode: str) -> float:
    weights = p.get("ethics_weights", {})
    mults = POLICY_MODES.get(mode, POLICY_MODES["default"])
    # Multiply each ethics channel, average simple
    num = 0.0; den = 0
    for k,v in weights.items():
        num += float(v) * float(mults.get(k,1.0)); den += 1
    return (num/den) if den>0 else 1.0
'''

if "MANIFEST_PATH" not in src:
    src = src.replace("TICK = 0", "TICK = 0\n" + insert_manifest)

# Modify _score_proj to include policy mode multiplier (if defined in Globals via env or request param)
src = src.replace(
    "def _score_proj(p: dict, bonuses: dict | None = None) -> float:",
    "def _score_proj(p: dict, bonuses: dict | None = None, mode: str = \"default\") -> float:"
)
src = src.replace(
    "def _rank_projects(seed: dict, bonuses: dict | None = None) -> list[dict]:",
    "def _rank_projects(seed: dict, bonuses: dict | None = None, mode: str = \"default\", role: str | None = None) -> list[dict]:"
)
src = src.replace(
    "s = _score_proj(p, bonuses=bonuses)",
    "s = _score_proj(p, bonuses=bonuses, mode=mode)"
)

# Inject role filter and policy mode into ranking
src = src.replace(
    "out = []\n    for p in seed.get(\"projects\", []):",
    "out = []\n    items = seed.get(\"projects\", [])\n    # role filter\n    if role and role in ROLE_FILTERS:\n        ftags = set(ROLE_FILTERS[role][\"tags\"])\n        items = [p for p in items if ftags & set([t.lower() for t in p.get(\"tags\",[])])]\n    for p in items:"
)

# Update projects_list endpoint to accept ?mode & ?role
src = src.replace(
    "def projects_list():\n    ranked = _rank_projects(SCORE_SEED, bonuses=_ACTIVITY)\n    return jsonify({\"count\": len(ranked), \"projects\": ranked})",
    "def projects_list():\n    from flask import request\n    mode = request.args.get(\"mode\",\"default\")\n    role = request.args.get(\"role\")\n    ranked = _rank_projects(SCORE_SEED, bonuses=_ACTIVITY, mode=mode, role=role)\n    return jsonify({\"count\": len(ranked), \"mode\": mode, \"role\": role, \"projects\": ranked})"
)

# Update projects_rescore to support mode & role
src = src.replace(
    "def projects_rescore():\n    # optional: override weights or bump activity\n    data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}\n    bump = data.get(\"bump\", {})  # {\"DRP-001\": 0.01}\n    for k,v in bump.items():\n        _activity_bump(k, float(v))\n    ranked = _rank_projects(SCORE_SEED, bonuses=_ACTIVITY)\n    sse_broadcast(\"project_scores\", {\"tick\": TICK, \"count\": len(ranked)})\n    return jsonify({\"count\": len(ranked), \"projects\": ranked})",
    "def projects_rescore():\n    data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}\n    bump = data.get(\"bump\", {})\n    mode = data.get(\"mode\",\"default\"); role = data.get(\"role\")\n    for k,v in bump.items(): _activity_bump(k, float(v))\n    ranked = _rank_projects(SCORE_SEED, bonuses=_ACTIVITY, mode=mode, role=role)\n    sse_broadcast(\"project_scores\", {\"tick\": TICK, \"count\": len(ranked), \"mode\": mode, \"role\": role})\n    return jsonify({\"count\": len(ranked), \"mode\": mode, \"role\": role, \"projects\": ranked})"
)

# Add manifest endpoints and ingest endpoint before __main__
extra_routes = r'''
@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/manifest", "/manifest", methods=["GET","POST"])
def manifest_rw():
    if request.method == "GET":
        return jsonify(_load_manifest())
    data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}
    m = _load_manifest()
    # shallow merge for simple fields
    for k,v in data.items():
        if k == "ingest_log":
            m.setdefault("ingest_log", []).extend(v if isinstance(v, list) else [v])
        else:
            m[k] = v
    _save_manifest(m)
    sse_broadcast("manifest_update", {"tick": TICK})
    return jsonify({"updated": True, "manifest": m})

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/ingest", "/ingest", methods=["POST"])
def ingest():
    # Accepts multipart/form-data file upload OR JSON {name, content (base64|text)}
    if request.files:
        f = request.files.get("file")
        if not f: return jsonify({"error":"no file"}), 400
        name = secure_filename(f.filename or f"artifact_{TICK}")
        path = os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "assets", name)
        f.save(path)
        log = {"path": f"tricore3/assets/{name}", "size": os.path.getsize(path), "ts": time.time()}
    else:
        data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}
        name = secure_filename(data.get("name","artifact.txt"))
        content = data.get("content","")
        path = os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "assets", name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.write(str(content))
        log = {"path": f"tricore3/assets/{name}", "size": os.path.getsize(path), "ts": time.time()}
    m = _load_manifest(); m.setdefault("ingest_log", []).append(log); _save_manifest(m)
    sse_broadcast("ingest", {"tick": TICK, "path": log["path"]})
    return jsonify({"ok": True, "stored": log})
'''
if extra_routes not in src:
    src = src.replace("if __name__ == \"__main__\":", extra_routes + "\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":")

with open(server_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(src)

# Minimal service worker + index

index_html = """<!doctype html><html><head>
<meta charset="utf-8"/><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"/>
<title>Möbii³us Auto-Ingest</title>
<link rel="manifest" href="/tricore3/pwa/manifest.webmanifest">

<style>body{background:#0a151c;color:#e8f5f9;font-family:system-ui;padding:16px}</style>
</head><body>
<h1>Mobii³us Auto-Ingest</h1>
<p>Use Android/iOS share to send files here. Or upload manually:</p>
<input id="f" type="file" multiple />
<button onclick="send()">Upload</button>
<pre id="out"></pre>
<script>
async function send(){
  const ff=document.getElementById('f'); const out=document.getElementById('out'); if(!ff.files.length){out.textContent='No files';return}
  const fd=new FormData(); for(const file of ff.files){ fd.append('file', file, file.name) }
  const r=await fetch('/tricore3/ingest',{method:'POST', body:fd}); const j=await r.json(); out.textContent=JSON.stringify(j,null,2);
}
</script>
</body></html>"""
with open(os.path.join(pwa_dir, "index.html"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(index_html)

# Add a simple Flask route to handle PWA share endpoint -> proxies to /ingest
with open(server_path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(r'''
@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/pwa", "/pwa", methods=["GET"])
def pwa_index():
    from flask import send_from_directory
    return send_from_directory(os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "pwa"), "index.html")

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/pwa/<path:fname>", methods=["GET"])
def pwa_static(fname):

    return send_from_directory(os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "pwa"), fname)

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/pwa/share", methods=["POST"])
def pwa_share():

    return ingest()
''')

# --- PWA & ingest ---
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/ingest", "/ingest", methods=["POST"])
def ingest():
    if request.files:
        f = request.files.get("file") or request.files.get("files")
        if not f: return jsonify({"error":"no file"}), 400
        name = secure_filename(f.filename or f"artifact_{int(time.time())}")
        path = os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "assets", name)
        f.save(path)
        log = {"path": f"tricore3/assets/{name}", "size": os.path.getsize(path), "ts": time.time()}
    else:
        data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}
        name = secure_filename(data.get("name","artifact.txt"))
        content = data.get("content","")
        path = os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "assets", name)
        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh: fh.write(str(content))
        log = {"path": f"tricore3/assets/{name}", "size": os.path.getsize(path), "ts": time.time()}
    m = _load_manifest(); m.setdefault("ingest_log", []).append(log); _save_manifest(m)
    sse_broadcast("ingest", {"tick": TICK, "path": log["path"]})
    return jsonify({"ok": True, "stored": log})

2) Manifest sync (read/write API)

Let the HUD & Active Buddy see and tag new artifacts instantly.

Add to server.py:

MANIFEST_PATH = os.path.join(BASE, "tricore3", "config", "manifest.json")

def _load_manifest():
    try:
        with open(MANIFEST_PATH, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f)
    except Exception: return {"meta":{"name":"root manifest","version":"0.0.1"},"ingest_log":[]}

def _save_manifest(m): 
    with open(MANIFEST_PATH, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump(m, f, indent=2)

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/manifest", "/manifest", methods=["GET","POST"])
def manifest_rw():
    if request.method == "GET": return jsonify(_load_manifest())
    data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}
    m = _load_manifest()
    for k,v in data.items():
        if k == "ingest_log": m.setdefault("ingest_log", []).extend(v if isinstance(v, list) else [v])
        else: m[k] = v
    _save_manifest(m); sse_broadcast("manifest_update", {"tick": TICK})
    return jsonify({"updated": True, "manifest": m})

3) Role dashboards (Field / Comms / Ops filters)

Expose role-filtered views right from the API; HUD and Buddy can switch.

Extend ranking to support ?role=:

ROLE_FILTERS = {
  "Field": {"tags":["field","hazards","geotech","hud","telemetry"]},
  "Comms": {"tags":["comms","ui","story","hud"]},
  "Ops":   {"tags":["ops","ledger","cred","infra","diagnostics"]},
}

def _rank_projects(seed, bonuses=None, mode="default", role=None):
    items = seed.get("projects", [])
    if role and role in ROLE_FILTERS:
        ftags = set(ROLE_FILTERS[role]["tags"])
        items = [p for p in items if ftags & set([t.lower() for t in p.get("tags",[])])]
    out = []
    for p in items:
        s = _score_proj(p, bonuses=bonuses, mode=mode)
        out.append({**p, "score": s})
    out.sort(key=lambda x: (-x["score"], x["priority"], x["id"]))
    for i,row in enumerate(out, start=1): row["rank"] = i
    return out

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/projects", "/projects", methods=["GET"])
def projects_list():
    mode = request.args.get("mode","default"); role = request.args.get("role")
    ranked = _rank_projects(SCORE_SEED, bonuses=_ACTIVITY, mode=mode, role=role)
    return jsonify({"count": len(ranked), "mode": mode, "role": role, "projects": ranked})

4) Policy-weighted scoring modes (Crisis / Growth / Justice)

Flip a mode, and we re-weight ethics channels per project before scoring.

Add to server.py:

POLICY_MODES = {
  "default":{"life":1.0,"property":1.0,"truth":1.0,"justice":1.0,"harm_min":1.0},
  "crisis":{"life":1.5,"property":1.2,"truth":1.1,"justice":1.0,"harm_min":1.3},
  "growth":{"life":1.0,"property":1.3,"truth":1.2,"justice":1.0,"harm_min":1.0},
  "justice":{"life":1.1,"property":1.0,"truth":1.0,"justice":1.4,"harm_min":1.2},
}

def _policy_weight_multiplier(p, mode):
    w = p.get("ethics_weights", {}); m = POLICY_MODES.get(mode, POLICY_MODES["default"])
    if not w: return 1.0
    return sum(float(w.get(k,0))*float(m.get(k,1)) for k in m)/len(m)

def _score_proj(p, bonuses=None, mode="default"):
    impact = float(p.get("impact_weight", 0.0))
    cred   = float(p.get("cred_weight", 0.0))
    effort = {"S":1.0,"M":2.0,"L":3.0}.get(str(p.get("effort","M")).upper()[0],2.0)
    bonus  = float((bonuses or {}).get(p.get("id"), 0.0))
    return (impact * cred * _policy_weight_multiplier(p, mode))/max(effort,0.5) + bonus

@multi_route(app, "/tricore3/projects/rescore", "/projects/rescore", methods=["POST"])
def projects_rescore():
    data = request.get_json(force=True, silent=True) or {}
    mode = data.get("mode","default"); role = data.get("role")
    for k,v in (data.get("bump",{}) or {}).items(): _activity_bump(k, float(v))
    ranked = _rank_projects(SCORE_SEED, bonuses=_ACTIVITY, mode=mode, role=role)
    sse_broadcast("project_scores", {"tick": TICK, "mode": mode, "role": role})
    return jsonify({"count": len(ranked), "mode": mode, "role": role, "projects": ranked})

oh yeah—got you. here’s a tight, working pattern that does all five in one go:

swap (hot-swap modules/devices)

teach (add vocab / concept mappings)

add (register new “old board” / rf / e-ink targets)

validate (self-check + loopbacks)

new server (push bubbles→pixels to many weird displays with almost no CPU on the client)


below is a single-file service you can paste and run. it’s intentionally tiny but extensible.


---

the “bubbles→pixels” edge server

what it does

treats each “bubble” as a pixel-tile (time-slice = texel), packs them into RGBA frames

routes frames to sinks:

rtp_sink → pipe to ffmpeg (hardware decode on old tv boards; zero app logic on device)

fb_sink → write raw frame to linux framebuffer (/dev/fb0) if you have it

eink_sink → write PBM/PGM partial updates (old e-readers over USB serial look like files)

rf_sink → just dumps I/Q or PCM into a named pipe (your modulator does the rest)


swap: hot-replace a sink or mapping

teach: learn a concept mapping: “word/gesture → RGB/command”

add: register a device + how it wants frames

validate: quick loopback: color bars + sink pings


> deps: fastapi, uvicorn, pydantic, numpy, Pillow



# run:  uvicorn server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5055
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, Body
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import json, time, os, io

app = FastAPI(title="Bubbles→Pixels Edge")

# ------------------------- state -------------------------
DEVICES: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}          # device_id -> {sink, params}
VOCAB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}            # term -> {color, cmd, meta}
SINKS: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}            # sink_id -> sink spec
MAPPINGS: Dict[str, str] = {}                    # concept -> sink_id
FRAME_W, FRAME_H = 64, 36                        # default tiny tile grid

# ------------------------- models -------------------------
class Device(BaseModel):
    device_id: str
    sink: str = Field(..., description="sink id to use")
    params: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Teach(BaseModel):
    term: str
    color: Optional[List[int]] = Field(default=None, description="RGB [0-255,0-255,0-255]")
    cmd: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="freeform command")
    meta: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Swap(BaseModel):
    concept: str
    sink: str

class Bubble(BaseModel):
    id: str
    t: float
    features: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    # you can also POST file payloads (audio/video) via /bubbles/upload

# ------------------------- sinks -------------------------
def _ensure_fifo(path: Path):
    if path.exists():
        return
    os.mkfifo(str(path))

def rtp_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Write raw RGB frames to a named pipe that ffmpeg picks up, e.g.:
    ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 -s 64x36 -r 15 -i /tmp/rtp_in \
           -c:v h264_v4l2m2m -f rtp rtp://<TV_BOARD_IP>:5004
    """
    fifo = Path(params.get("fifo", "/tmp/rtp_in"))
    _ensure_fifo(fifo)
    with open(fifo, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(frame.astype(np.uint8).tobytes(order="C"))

def fb_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Push to Linux framebuffer (/dev/fb0). Set size/depth beforehand (or use kmsdrm).
    """
    dev = params.get("dev", "/dev/fb0")
    # convert to BGRX if needed; here we just dump RGB24
    with open(dev, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(frame.astype(np.uint8).tobytes(order="C"))

def eink_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Old e-readers: write 1-bit PBM or 8-bit PGM to a mount/serial device;
    the device firmware script handles refresh. Minimal CPU on device.
    """
    mode = params.get("mode", "pgm")  # "pbm" or "pgm"
    out = Path(params.get("out", "/tmp/eink_frame.pgm"))
    img = Image.fromarray(frame.astype(np.uint8), mode="RGB").convert("L")
    if mode == "pbm":
        img = img.point(lambda p: 255 if p > 128 else 0).convert("1")
        img.save(out, format="PPM")  # PBM/PGM/PPM are Netpbm: Pillow uses PPM for >1-bit; OK for most firmware
    else:
        img.save(out, format="PPM")  # grayscale in PPM works broadly

def rf_sink(samples: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    """
    Dump PCM/IQ float32 to pipe; downstream SDR/modulator handles RF.
    """
    fifo = Path(params.get("fifo", "/tmp/rf_in"))
    _ensure_fifo(fifo)
    with open(fifo, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(samples.astype(np.float32).tobytes(order="C"))

SINK_FUNS = {
    "rtp": rtp_sink,
    "fb": fb_sink,
    "eink": eink_sink,
    "rf": rf_sink,
}

# ------------------------- helpers -------------------------
def term_to_rgb(term: str) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    universal concepts-translator (toy): map a term to RGB.
    learned mapping wins; else hash -> stable color; fall back to gray.
    """
    t = term.lower().strip()
    if t in VOCAB and VOCAB[t].get("color"):
        r,g,b = VOCAB[t]["color"]
        return np.array([r,g,b], dtype=np.uint8)
    h = abs(hash(t)) & 0xFFFFFF
    return np.array([(h>>16)&255, (h>>8)&255, h&255], dtype=np.uint8)

def bubbles_to_frame(bubbles: List[Bubble], w=FRAME_W, h=FRAME_H) -> np.ndarray:
    """
    pack bubbles into a tiny RGB frame (w*h). each bubble is a pixel tile colored by concept.
    """
    frame = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    if not bubbles:
        return frame
    # place by time order; wrap around
    for i, b in enumerate(bubbles):
        x, y = (i % w), (i // w) % h
        concept = b.features.get("concept") or b.features.get("term") or "bubble"
        frame[y, x, :] = term_to_rgb(concept)
    return frame

def color_bars(w=FRAME_W, h=FRAME_H) -> np.ndarray:
    cols = [
        (255,255,255),(255,255,0),(0,255,255),(0,255,0),(255,0,255),(255,0,0),(0,0,255)
    ]
    seg = max(1, w//len(cols))
    img = np.zeros((h,w,3), dtype=np.uint8)
    for i,c in enumerate(cols):
        img[:, i*seg:(i+1)*seg, :] = np.array(c, dtype=np.uint8)
    return img

# ------------------------- routes -------------------------
@app.post("/add")
def add_device(d: Device):
    DEVICES[d.device_id] = {"sink": d.sink, "params": d.params, "added": time.time()}
    return {"ok": True, "devices": list(DEVICES.keys())}

@app.post("/teach")
def teach(t: Teach):
    VOCAB[t.term] = {"color": t.color, "cmd": t.cmd, "meta": t.meta, "t": time.time()}
    return {"ok": True, "learned": t.term}

@app.post("/swap")
def swap(s: Swap):
    MAPPINGS[s.concept] = s.sink
    return {"ok": True, "concept": s.concept, "sink": s.sink}

@app.get("/validate")
def validate():
    # 1) confirm at least one sink
    sinks = list(SINK_FUNS.keys())
    # 2) make a color bar frame
    test_frame = color_bars()
    # 3) dry-run sinks present in DEVICES (no exceptions)
    notes = []
    for did, meta in DEVICES.items():
        sink_id = meta["sink"]
        fn = SINK_FUNS.get(sink_id)
        try:
            if sink_id == "rf":
                fn(np.random.randn(4800).astype(np.float32), meta["params"])
            else:
                fn(test_frame, meta["params"])
            notes.append(f"{did}:{sink_id}=ok")
        except Exception as e:
            notes.append(f"{did}:{sink_id}=err({e})")
    return {"ok": True, "sinks": sinks, "devices_checked": notes}

@app.post("/bubbles/push")
def bubbles_push(payload: Dict[str, Any] = Body(...)):
    """
    Accepts a list: { bubbles: [ {id,t,features:{term/concept}}... ], route:{device_id? sink?}}
    Packs to a frame and forwards to the chosen sink or device.
    """
    bubbles = [Bubble(**b) for b in payload.get("bubbles", [])]
    route = payload.get("route", {})
    frame = bubbles_to_frame(bubbles)

    # choose target
    if "device_id" in route:
        meta = DEVICES.get(route["device_id"])
        if not meta: return {"ok": False, "error": "unknown device"}
        sink_id, params = meta["sink"], meta["params"]
    else:
        sink_id = route.get("sink", "rtp")
        params = route.get("params", {})

    fn = SINK_FUNS.get(sink_id)
    if not fn:
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"unknown sink '{sink_id}'"}
    if sink_id == "rf":
        # turn frame to mono PCM (very silly placeholder)
        pcm = frame.mean(axis=2).astype(np.float32).flatten() / 255.0
        fn(pcm, params)
    else:
        fn(frame, params)
    return {"ok": True, "pixels": int(frame.size/3)}

@app.post("/bubbles/upload")
async def bubbles_upload(file: UploadFile, concept: str = "bubble"):
    """
    Accept raw clips (webm/mp4/wav). We don't decode; we just log & map 'concept' → color/command.
    Old TV boards do hw decode via the RTP path; this endpoint is just bookkeeping.
    """
    data = await file.read()
    out = Path("/tmp")/f"bubble_{int(time.time()*1000)}_{file.filename}"
    out.write_bytes(data)
    # “teach” a mapping stub if unknown
    if concept not in VOCAB:
        VOCAB[concept] = {"color": None, "cmd": "play", "meta": {"src": str(out)}}
    return {"ok": True, "stored": str(out), "concept": concept}

@app.get("/state")
def state():
    return {
        "devices": DEVICES,
        "vocab": VOCAB,
        "mappings": MAPPINGS,
        "frame": {"w": FRAME_W, "h": FRAME_H}
    }


---

how this maps to your ask

swap: POST /swap { "concept": "alert", "sink": "eink" }
instantly reroutes anything labeled “alert” to the e-ink wall (no math, no rebuild).

teach: POST /teach { "term": "door_open", "color": [255,80,0], "cmd":"flash" }
now any bubble with features.term="door_open" paints that color (and you can use cmd downstream).

add: POST /add { "device_id":"tv-livingroom", "sink":"rtp", "params":{"fifo":"/tmp/rtp_in"}}

validate: GET /validate pings sinks with color bars + RF noise. If your old TV board is listening via ffmpeg, it lights up.

new server: the FastAPI app above. No special hardware on the clients—just ffmpeg or a tiny script that reads PBM/PPM on the e-reader, or an SDR script reading the RF FIFO.



---

wiring old tv boards (zero app logic)

On the TV board (Linux SOC with V4L2/VAAPI/NVDEC/etc), run:

# 1) create the input pipe once
mkfifo /tmp/rtp_in

# 2) transcode and send (hardware encoder if present)
ffmpeg -f rawvideo -pix_fmt rgb24 -s 64x36 -r 15 -i /tmp/rtp_in \
  -vf "scale=1280:720:flags=fast_bilinear" \
  -c:v h264_v4l2m2m -b:v 1M -f rtp rtp://127.0.0.1:5004

That’s it. The board just decodes what we push. No CPU spent on app logic.


---

e-ink (etch-a-sketch mode)

On an old e-reader (serial gadget or mass-storage):

mount /tmp/eink_frame.pgm from the server or sync it over USB

a tiny device script does eips -g eink_frame.pgm (Kindle) or an fbink call

the server only writes a single grayscale image; device handles refresh policy



---

rf (no-cpu display)

This server dumps mono PCM/IQ to /tmp/rf_in

Your modulator (HackRF/Pluto or even a cheap NTSC mod) turns it into analog carrier → old TVs display a pulsing tile field

Swap the mapping to broadcast only the tiles you care about



---

quick smoke tests (curl)

# add two devices
curl -X POST localhost:5055/add -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"device_id":"tv1","sink":"rtp","params":{"fifo":"/tmp/rtp_in"}}'

curl -X POST localhost:5055/add -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"device_id":"slate1","sink":"eink","params":{"out":"/tmp/eink_frame.pgm","mode":"pgm"}}'

# teach colors
curl -X POST localhost:5055/teach -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"term":"ok","color":[0,200,120]}'
curl -X POST localhost:5055/teach -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"term":"alert","color":[255,60,40]}'

# push bubbles to the TV
curl -X POST localhost:5055/bubbles/push -H "content-type: application/json" -d '{
  "bubbles":[
    {"id":"b1","t":0,"features":{"term":"ok"}},
    {"id":"b2","t":1,"features":{"term":"alert"}},
    {"id":"b3","t":2,"features":{"term":"ok"}}
  ],
  "route":{"device_id":"tv1"}
}'

# route alerts to e-ink instead
curl -X POST localhost:5055/swap -H "content-type: application/json" \
  -d '{"concept":"alert","sink":"eink"}'


---

why “bubbles as pixels” works (no math version)

treat each bubble as a symbol → assign a color (or 1-bit on/off) with the concept translator

pack symbols into a tiny grid; let the hardware decoder / display scaler stretch it

old GPUs/codecs on TV boards do the heavy lift; we only feed a FIFO

e-readers update from a single PBM/PGM file; no CPU loop on device

RF path carries the same tiles as amplitude or frequency changes; a whole wall of CRTs can show your state without a single app installed



---

next tiny adds (say the word and I’ll drop them in)

RTP server mode (skip ffmpeg pipe; use aiortc for direct H264)

tile addressability (send commands to a tile index → blink / invert on device via simple LUT)

concept stacks (layers: urgency, ownership, location → fused into a color)

device groups (route: {"group":"north_wall"})

# Create a ready-to-run "bubbles→pixels" edge server package with tricore³ wiring and a tiny dashboard.
import os, json, zipfile, textwrap, pathlib, hashlib, datetime

ROOT = "/mnt/data/bubbles_pixels_edge_v0_1"
os.makedirs(ROOT, exist_ok=True)

server_py = r'''# bubbles→pixels edge server (v0.1) — with tricore³ wiring
# run: uvicorn server:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 5055
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, Body
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, HTMLResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Dict, Any, List, Optional
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image
import json, time, os, io, requests, base64

app = FastAPI(title="Bubbles→Pixels Edge")

# ------------------------- state -------------------------
DEVICES: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}          # device_id -> {sink, params}
VOCAB: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}            # term -> {color, cmd, meta}
SINKS: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}            # sink_id -> sink spec
MAPPINGS: Dict[str, str] = {}                    # concept -> sink_id
FRAME_W, FRAME_H = int(os.getenv("BPX_W", 64)), int(os.getenv("BPX_H", 36))

TRICORE_BASE = os.getenv("TRICORE_BASE", "http://127.0.0.1:5059")
TRICORE_BUMP = float(os.getenv("TRICORE_BUMP", "0.005"))

# ------------------------- models -------------------------
class Device(BaseModel):
    device_id: str
    sink: str = Field(..., description="sink id to use (rtp|fb|eink|rf)")
    params: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Teach(BaseModel):
    term: str
    color: Optional[List[int]] = Field(default=None, description="RGB [0-255,0-255,0-255]")
    cmd: Optional[str] = Field(default=None, description="freeform command")
    meta: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

class Swap(BaseModel):
    concept: str
    sink: str

class Bubble(BaseModel):
    id: str
    t: float
    features: Dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)

# ------------------------- sinks -------------------------
def _ensure_fifo(path: Path):
    if path.exists():
        return
    os.mkfifo(str(path))

def rtp_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    fifo = Path(params.get("fifo", "/tmp/rtp_in"))
    _ensure_fifo(fifo)
    with open(fifo, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(frame.astype(np.uint8).tobytes(order="C"))

def fb_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    dev = params.get("dev", "/dev/fb0")
    with open(dev, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(frame.astype(np.uint8).tobytes(order="C"))

def eink_sink(frame: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    mode = params.get("mode", "pgm")  # "pbm" or "pgm"
    out = Path(params.get("out", "/tmp/eink_frame.pgm"))
    img = Image.fromarray(frame.astype(np.uint8), mode="RGB").convert("L")
    if mode == "pbm":
        img = img.point(lambda p: 255 if p > 128 else 0).convert("1")
        img.save(out, format="PPM")
    else:
        img.save(out, format="PPM")

def rf_sink(samples: np.ndarray, params: Dict[str, Any]):
    fifo = Path(params.get("fifo", "/tmp/rf_in"))
    _ensure_fifo(fifo)
    with open(fifo, "wb", buffering=0) as f:
        f.write(samples.astype(np.float32).tobytes(order="C"))

SINK_FUNS = {"rtp": rtp_sink, "fb": fb_sink, "eink": eink_sink, "rf": rf_sink}

# ------------------------- helpers -------------------------
def term_to_rgb(term: str) -> np.ndarray:
    t = str(term).lower().strip()
    if t in VOCAB and VOCAB[t].get("color"):
        r,g,b = VOCAB[t]["color"]
        return np.array([r,g,b], dtype=np.uint8)
    h = abs(hash(t)) & 0xFFFFFF
    return np.array([(h>>16)&255, (h>>8)&255, h&255], dtype=np.uint8)

def bubbles_to_frame(bubbles: List[Bubble], w=FRAME_W, h=FRAME_H) -> np.ndarray:
    frame = np.zeros((h, w, 3), dtype=np.uint8)
    if not bubbles: return frame
    for i, b in enumerate(bubbles):
        x, y = (i % w), (i // w) % h
        concept = b.features.get("concept") or b.features.get("term") or "bubble"
        frame[y, x, :] = term_to_rgb(concept)
    return frame

def color_bars(w=FRAME_W, h=FRAME_H) -> np.ndarray:
    cols = [(255,255,255),(255,255,0),(0,255,255),(0,255,0),(255,0,255),(255,0,0),(0,0,255)]
    seg = max(1, w//len(cols))
    img = np.zeros((h,w,3), dtype=np.uint8)
    for i,c in enumerate(cols):
        img[:, i*seg:(i+1)*seg, :] = np.array(c, dtype=np.uint8)
    return img

def _tricore_ingest_note(title: str):
    try:
        requests.post(f"{TRICORE_BASE}/tricore3/manifest", json={"notes":[{"title":title,"ts":time.time()}]}, timeout=1.5)
    except Exception: pass

def _tricore_bump_by_terms(terms: List[str]):
    # naive: bump projects whose tags intersect with terms
    if not terms: return
    try:
        # fetch projects and match tags locally
        pr = requests.get(f"{TRICORE_BASE}/tricore3/projects", timeout=2.0).json()
        bump = {}
        for p in pr.get("projects", []):
            tags = [str(t).lower() for t in (p.get("tags") or [])]
            if set(t.lower() for t in terms) & set(tags):
                bump[p.get("id")] = TRICORE_BUMP
        if bump:
            requests.post(f"{TRICORE_BASE}/tricore3/projects/rescore", json={"bump": bump}, timeout=1.5)
    except Exception:
        pass

# ------------------------- routes -------------------------
@app.get("/", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def home():
    return """<html><head><title>Bubbles→Pixels</title>
<style>body{background:#0a151c;color:#e8f5f9;font-family:system-ui;padding:16px} pre{background:#0b1a22;border:1px solid #1a3344;border-radius:8px;padding:12px}</style>
</head><body>
<h2>🫧 → 🧩 Bubbles→Pixels Edge</h2>
<p>swap / teach / add / validate / push. <a href="/dash">Open dashboard</a></p>
<pre>curl -s localhost:5055/state | jq</pre>
</body></html>"""

@app.get("/dash", response_class=HTMLResponse)
def dash():
    return """<!doctype html><meta charset=utf-8>
<title>Bubbles→Pixels Dashboard</title>
<style>body{background:#0a151c;color:#e8f5f9;font-family:system-ui;padding:16px} canvas{background:#07131a;border:1px solid #1a3344;border-radius:8px}</style>
<h3>Live Frame</h3>
<canvas id="c" width="640" height="360"></canvas>
<script>
async function draw(){ const r = await fetch('/frame.png?_=' + Date.now()); const b = await r.blob(); const url = URL.createObjectURL(b);
 const img = new Image(); img.onload = ()=>{ const k=document.getElementById('c'); const ctx=k.getContext('2d'); ctx.drawImage(img,0,0,k.width,k.height); URL.revokeObjectURL(url)}; img.src=url; }
setInterval(draw, 500); draw();
</script>
"""

@app.get("/frame.png")
def frame_png():
    img = Image.fromarray(color_bars())
    buf = io.BytesIO(); img = img.resize((FRAME_W*10, FRAME_H*10), Image.NEAREST); img.save(buf, format="PNG"); buf.seek(0)
    return FileResponse(buf, media_type="image/png")

@app.post("/add")
def add_device(d: Device):
    DEVICES[d.device_id] = {"sink": d.sink, "params": d.params, "added": time.time()}
    return {"ok": True, "devices": list(DEVICES.keys())}

@app.post("/teach")
def teach(t: Teach):
    VOCAB[t.term] = {"color": t.color, "cmd": t.cmd, "meta": t.meta, "t": time.time()}
    _tricore_ingest_note(f"teach:{t.term}")
    return {"ok": True, "learned": t.term}

@app.post("/teach/bulk")
def teach_bulk(ts: List[Teach]):
    for t in ts:
        VOCAB[t.term] = {"color": t.color, "cmd": t.cmd, "meta": t.meta, "t": time.time()}
    _tricore_ingest_note(f"teach:{len(ts)} terms")
    return {"ok": True, "learned": len(ts)}

@app.post("/swap")
def swap(s: Swap):
    MAPPINGS[s.concept] = s.sink
    _tricore_ingest_note(f"swap:{s.concept}->{s.sink}")
    return {"ok": True, "concept": s.concept, "sink": s.sink}

@app.get("/validate")
def validate():
    sinks = list(SINK_FUNS.keys())
    test_frame = color_bars()
    notes = []
    for did, meta in DEVICES.items():
        sink_id = meta["sink"]; fn = SINK_FUNS.get(sink_id)
        try:
            if sink_id == "rf":
                fn(np.random.randn(4800).astype(np.float32), meta["params"])
            else:
                fn(test_frame, meta["params"])
            notes.append(f"{did}:{sink_id}=ok")
        except Exception as e:
            notes.append(f"{did}:{sink_id}=err({e})")
    return {"ok": True, "sinks": sinks, "devices_checked": notes}

@app.post("/bubbles/push")
def bubbles_push(payload: Dict[str, Any] = Body(...)):
    bubbles = [Bubble(**b) for b in payload.get("bubbles", [])]
    route = payload.get("route", {})
    frame = bubbles_to_frame(bubbles)
    terms = [b.features.get("concept") or b.features.get("term") for b in bubbles if b.features]

    # choose target
    if "device_id" in route:
        meta = DEVICES.get(route["device_id"])
        if not meta: return {"ok": False, "error": "unknown device"}
        sink_id, params = meta["sink"], meta["params"]
    else:
        sink_id = route.get("sink", "rtp")
        params = route.get("params", {})

    fn = SINK_FUNS.get(sink_id)
    if not fn:
        return {"ok": False, "error": f"unknown sink '{sink_id}'"}
    if sink_id == "rf":
        pcm = frame.mean(axis=2).astype(np.float32).flatten() / 255.0
        fn(pcm, params)
    else:
        fn(frame, params)

    # tricore bump on concepts
    _tricore_bump_by_terms([t for t in terms if t])

    return {"ok": True, "pixels": int(frame.size/3), "sink": sink_id}

@app.post("/bubbles/upload")
async def bubbles_upload(file: UploadFile, concept: str = "bubble"):
    data = await file.read()
    out = Path("/tmp")/f"bubble_{int(time.time()*1000)}_{file.filename}"
    out.write_bytes(data)
    if concept not in VOCAB:
        VOCAB[concept] = {"color": None, "cmd": "play", "meta": {"src": str(out)}}
    # forward a manifest note to tricore
    _tricore_ingest_note(f"upload:{file.filename} concept:{concept}")
    return {"ok": True, "stored": str(out), "concept": concept}

@app.get("/state")
def state():
    return {"devices": DEVICES, "vocab": VOCAB, "mappings": MAPPINGS, "frame": {"w": FRAME_W, "h": FRAME_H}, "tricore_base": TRICORE_BASE}
'''
open(os.path.join(ROOT, "server.py"), "w", encoding="utf-8").write(server_py)

readme = f"""# Bubbles→Pixels Edge (v0.1)

Swap • Teach • Add • Validate • New Server — **in one file** (`server.py`).

- **teach**: POST `/teach` (or `/teach/bulk`) adds concept→RGB/command

"""

- It shows WHO needs to talk to WHO in what order so the transfer can actually happen.

—————————

## 2. Packaging for storefronts + costs  
   
### App store mechanics  
   
**Apple (iOS)**  
   
   
- Annual developer program fee: **$99/year**.  
   
- Commission on digital goods/services sold in-app: **30%**, or **15%** under the Small Business Program (sub-$1M revenue).  
   
  
   
**Google Play (Android)**  
   
   
- One-time developer registration fee: **$25 USD**.  
   
- Service fee: typically **15% for the first $1M** yearly, **30% above** that for digital goods.  
   
  
   
For **your use case** (Torah/Noahide education, donation links going through web), a lot of revenue can stay *off* in-app purchase rails; that means:  
   
   
- Apps are free on stores.  
   
- Donations / sponsorships go via web checkout (Stripe/PayPal/etc.), avoiding the 15–30% cuts.  
   
  
   
### Backend hosting (realistic starter numbers)  
   
A modest global pilot (few thousand users, mostly text + some audio) can run on:  
   
   
- 1–2 small VPS instances (DigitalOcean, Hetzner, etc.).   
   
  - Example: DO basic droplet, 1 vCPU / 1GB RAM is about **$6/month**; 2 vCPU / 4GB is about **$24/month**.  
   
  
   
   
- Managed DB or a single Postgres container (~$10–60/month depending on provider).  
   
- Object storage for logs / TOFAR / audio (≈$5–20/month entry scale).  
   
  
   
Rough ballpark for a **serious but small** deployment:  
   
   
- **Barebones**: $30–70/month (1 VPS + DB + backups).  
   
- **Comfortable**: $100–250/month (2–3 VPS for redundancy, DB, storage, monitoring).  
   
  
   
You can truthfully tell them: **infra is in the hundreds per month, not tens of thousands**. The real investment is *people* and *content supervision*, which is exactly their lane.

The system, called **Möbii⁴ / Buddy**, is designed so that *every* person, device, and text becomes a **Member** in a single, ethical lattice, with clear boundaries and full provenance.  
    
**2. Core idea in one paragraph**  
   
Buddy treats people, devices, and even letters as **Members**, each with an ID and coordinates in a “fractal map.” Members move through three streams:  
   
   
- **ToyStream** – internal tests and simulations  
   
- **FieldStream** – real-world evidence and usage  
   
- **ContextStream** – roles, halachic guardrails, personal preferences  
   
  
   
A **Fractal Coordinator** chooses *what to do* and *how fast* (“Two Derivatives”), while a **Guardian** layer enforces ethics and consent with **TOFAR** logging. All actions, especially RF/IR and content generation, are constrained by halachic policy, law, and explicit consent.  
   
The system is **offline-first**, runs on small devices, and uses the cloud only as needed.  
    
**3. Alignment with Ask Noah & Chabad**  
   
   
- **Ethics-first architecture** – Guardian + TOFAR are not bolted on; they are **the first gate** and are parameterized explicitly by the Seven Noahide Laws and The Divine Code.  
   
- **Human rabbinic authority** – Any answer that hits defined “red lines” (psak, controversial halacha, life-and-death decisions) is **deferred**, marked with TOFAR, and routed to a human rabbi rather than guessed by the system.  
   
- **No ad-tech, no data sale** – The system is not a business model based on attention or profiling. Data is minimized, anonymized where possible, and never sold. It is a **tool of service**, not a funnel.  
   
  
    
**4. What Buddy can do for Ask Noah & 770**  
   
**a) Personal Noahide Companion**  
   
   
- 24/7 question-answering focused on **Divine Code / Seven Gates / Ask Noah materials**, with citations and links to primary texts.  
   
- Gentle learning plans (“7 minutes for the 7 laws”) with reminders, review questions, and encouragement.  
   
- Multi-language rollout (starting with English, expanding to languages where Ask Noah already has content and translators).  
   
  
   
**b) Educator / Shliach Tools**  
   
   
- “Buddy Classroom” mode for rabbis, teachers, and shluchim:   
   
  - Build lessons from canonical content, with all sources tracked.  
   
  - Generate quizzes, handouts, and summaries at different reading levels.  
   
  - Offline use in places with poor connectivity; syncs when back online.  
   
  
   
   
  
   
**c) Content Stewardship for Ask Noah**  
   
   
- Structured ingestion of existing and future works (The Divine Code, Seven Gates of Righteous Knowledge, articles and Q&As).  
   
- Every generated explanation or answer can be traced back to **which paragraphs of which books** were used, via TOFAR.  
   
- Drafting tools for new editions, children’s versions, and small flyers—always marked as drafts for human rabbinic review.  
   
  
   
**d) Visibility into Global Questions (without exposing private lives)**  
   
   
- 770 / Ask Noah Console:   
   
  - Aggregated view of what the world is asking about Noahide law and basic Jewish faith, grouped by topic and geography.  
   
  - No individual identities shown, only trends: “Many questions about family law in region X,” etc.  
   
  - Helps prioritize translations, new chapters, and outreach efforts.  
   
  
   
   
  
   
**e) Technical Safeguards**  
   
   
- RF/IR/SDR actions: strictly owner-scoped and rate-limited, and constrained to legally allowed device functions and bands in each jurisdiction.  
   
- Full consent ledger: who permitted which functions, when, and with what scope.  
   
- Stream configurations and Guardian rules are exportable for independent review.  
   
  
    
**5. Phased plan**  
   
**Phase 1 – Closed Pilot (3–6 months)**  
   
   
- Scope: Ask Noah staff + a small group of trusted shluchim and educators.  
   
- Deliverables:   
   
  - Noahide Q&A companion (web + Android beta).  
   
  - Console for staff to review TOFAR logs, moderate content, and refine guardrails.  
   
  
   
   
- Outputs:   
   
  - Measured accuracy vs. canonical texts.  
   
  - User feedback on clarity, tone, and usefulness.  
   
  
   
   
  
   
**Phase 2 – Wider Noahide Rollout (6–18 months)**  
   
   
- Scope: Global English-speaking Noahides and interested non-Jews.  
   
- Features:   
   
  - Translation support for priority languages.  
   
  - Classroom Buddy for community classes, online and offline.  
   
  
   
   
- Governance: joint committee (Ask Noah + technical team) for ongoing guardrails.  
   
  
   
**Phase 3 – Chabad House Integration**  
   
   
- Optional deeper integration with Chabad Houses worldwide:   
   
  - Standardized educational flows for guests and regulars.  
   
  - Optional “house-branded” skins, while keeping the same Guardian core.  
   
  - Periodic reports to 770 on learning trends, challenges, and successes.  
   
  
   
   
  
    
**6. Costs & requested partnership**  
   
Technical infrastructure costs for a serious pilot are **hundreds of dollars per month**, not more, using commodity VPS hosting and open-source models where possible.  
   
The real cost is:  
   
   
- Ongoing technical maintenance and development.  
   
- Content ingestion and rabbinic supervision.  
   
- Translation and community support.  
   
  
   
The ask is **not** for a blank check, but for:  
   
   
1. **Formal rabbinic oversight and guidance** from Ask Noah / designated poskim.  
   
2. **Permission to present Buddy explicitly as aligned with The Divine Code and Ask Noah.**  
   
3. A discussion about partial funding or in-kind support for the pilot phase (for example, sponsoring infra + a modest developer/content budget).  
   
  
   
The intent is that **ownership and moral steering remain firmly within Torah-true institutions**, and the technology remains a tool in their hands.  
   
Respectfully submitted,

Buddy is built on **portioning**:     For every event:     - *What part helps us?*   - *What part marks a boundary?*   - *What part can this person actually use right now?*        The same event is seen three ways:     - **Reservoir** – the part we keep and learn from   - **Floodplain** – the part that shows us the edge of what’s safe/allowed   - **User** – the part we phrase as: “Here’s what we *can* do”      Nothing is discarded. Nothing is demonized. Everything is **placed** where it belongs.   This rule—**Both Sides Win**—is the heart of Buddy. Installing Buddy means agreeing that this is how events are handled from now on.   The rest of the manual is just: *how we do that in your context*.    # 5. The Fullerene Selector (How Buddy Chooses a Face)   Inside the engine, Buddy uses something we call the **Fullerene kernel**.   You don’t need to know the math to use it, but you should know what it *does*:     - It treats your system as a **ball of connected facets** (faces).   - Each facet represents a perspective: safety, performance, fairness, cost, comfort, etc.   - The **Fullerene selector** is the part that decides *which facet to show right now*.      When an event arrives, the selector doesn’t ask:     “Is this good or bad?”     It asks:     “Which face needs to be facing this event first so everyone benefits?”     Examples:     - For a **safety-critical event**, the “ethics / risk” face leads; performance yields.   - For a **routine optimization**, the “efficiency / speed” face leads; comfort yields.   - For a **user distress signal**, the “compassion / clarity” face leads; complexity yields.      Install, in Fullerene terms, means:     - loading the kernel,   - telling it which faces you care about,   - and letting the selector pick the right one per event.      Whenever you see “Fullerene selector” in this documentation, you can mentally read:     “The system’s way of choosing which value to honor first, without throwing the others away.”      # 6. The Monitors (How You See What Buddy Sees)   Because Buddy is constantly portioning events and shifting faces, you need a way to:     - **see what’s happening**,   - **see why it happened**, and   - **see whether it’s healthy**.      That’s where the monitors come in.   At a high level, Buddy’s monitor layer gives you:     -   **Guardian view** Is this action allowed, asking for consent, or blocked—for what reason?     -   **Health view** Are events being portioned smoothly, or are we seeing spikes in boundary hits, delays, or failures?     -   **Analysis view** For a given event, what did Buddy send to Reservoir, to Floodplain, and to the User?        All of that is derived from the same install:     1. Events go in.   2. Both Sides Win portioning runs.   3. Fullerene face selection happens.   4. Monitors show what was chosen and why.      The point of the monitor is not to overwhelm you with numbers. It’s to give you **explanations that match how humans actually talk**:     - “We softened this.”   - “We redirected that.”   - “We declined this, and here’s a safer alternative we offered instead.”       # 7. Quick Install: The Three Moves   Whether you’re using Buddy as:     - a product (TinyBox, web app),   - a platform (APIs, services), or   - an engine (Fullerene + monitor + analysis),      the install is always the same three moves.   ### 7.1. Declare a HOME Node   Pick the first place Buddy lives.   That might be:     - a single laptop,   - a specific server,   - a TinyBox on a counter, or   - a named workspace in the cloud.      For our examples, we call it:     **HOME-001**     This is where Buddy’s memory, ethics, and logs anchor unless you explicitly change it.   ### 7.2. Define Your Events   Tell Buddy **what counts as “something happened”**.   For example:     - “A user submits a request”   - “A sensor crosses a threshold”   - “A job fails to complete”   - “A person asks for help”   - “A script touches protected data”      The system doesn’t assume. You name the events; Buddy handles them.   ### 7.3. Turn On Both Sides Win   Finally, you enable Buddy’s default handling rule:     **Every event is portioned into useful truth, boundary truth, and actionable truth. All sides get what they need. No hard discard. No silent fail.**     Once that is on:     - the Fullerene selector chooses the right facet,   - the monitors begin to reflect real structure,   - the analysis layer starts explaining decisions, and   - users see responses that feel *helpful*, not hostile. The Core Idea: Both Sides Win   Most systems are built on **binary choices**:     - allow / block   - pass / fail   - in / out   - win / lose      Buddy is not.   Buddy is built on **portioning**:     For every event:     - *What part helps us?*   - *What part marks a boundary?*   - *What part can this person actually use right now?*        The same event is seen three ways:     - **Reservoir** – the part we keep and learn from   - **Floodplain** – the part that shows us the edge of what’s safe/allowed   - **User** – the part we phrase as: “Here’s what we *can* do”      Nothing is discarded. The Fullerene Selector (How Buddy Chooses a Face)   Inside the engine, Buddy uses something we call the **Fullerene kernel**.   You don’t need to know the math to use it, but you should know what it *does*:     - It treats your system as a **ball of connected facets** (faces).   - Each facet represents a perspective: safety, performance, fairness, cost, comfort, etc.   - The **Fullerene selector** is the part that decides *which facet to show right now*.      When an event arrives, the selector doesn’t ask:     “Is this good or bad?”     It asks:     “Which face needs to be facing this event first so everyone benefits?”     Examples:     - For a **safety-critical event**, the “ethics / risk” face leads; performance yields.   - For a **routine optimization**, the “efficiency / speed” face leads; comfort yields.   - For a **user distress signal**, the “compassion / clarity” face leads; complexity yields.      Install, in Fullerene terms, means:     - loading the kernel,   - telling it which faces you care about,   - and letting the selector pick the right one per event.      Whenever you see “Fullerene selector” in this documentation, you can mentally read:     “The system’s way of choosing which value to honor first, without throwing the others away.”      # 6. The Monitors (How You See What Buddy Sees)   Because Buddy is constantly portioning events and shifting faces, you need a way to:     - **see what’s happening**,   - **see why it happened**, and   - **see whether it’s healthy**.      That’s where the monitors come in.   At a high level, Buddy’s monitor layer gives you:     -   **Guardian view** Is this action allowed, asking for consent, or blocked—for what reason?     -   **Health view** Are events being portioned smoothly, or are we seeing spikes in boundary hits, delays, or failures?     -   **Analysis view** For a given event, what did Buddy send to Reservoir, to Floodplain, and to the User?        All of that is derived from the same install:     1. Events go in.   2. Both Sides Win portioning runs.   3. Fullerene face selection happens.   4. Monitors show what was chosen and why.      The point of the monitor is not to overwhelm you with numbers. It’s to give you **explanations that match how humans actually talk**:     - “We softened this.”   - “We redirected that.”   - “We declined this, and here’s a safer alternative we offered instead.”       # 7. Quick Install: The Three Moves   Whether you’re using Buddy as:     - a product (TinyBox, web app),   - a platform (APIs, services), or   - an engine (Fullerene + monitor + analysis),      the install is always the same three moves.   ### 7.1. Declare a HOME Node   Pick the first place Buddy lives.   That might be:     - a single laptop,   - a specific server,   - a TinyBox on a counter, or   - a named workspace in the cloud.      For our examples, we call it:     **HOME-001**     This is where Buddy’s memory, ethics, and logs anchor unless you explicitly change it.   ### 7.2. Define Your Events   Tell Buddy **what counts as “something happened”**.   For example:     - “A user submits a request”   - “A sensor crosses a threshold”   - “A job fails to complete”   - “A person asks for help”   - “A script touches protected data”      The system doesn’t assume. You name the events; Buddy handles them.   ### 7.3. Turn On Both Sides Win   Finally, you enable Buddy’s default handling rule:     **Every event is portioned into useful truth, boundary truth, and actionable truth. All sides get what they need. No hard discard. No silent fail.**     Once that is on:     - the Fullerene selector chooses the right facet,   - the monitors begin to reflect real structure,   - the analysis layer starts explaining decisions, and   - users see responses that feel *helpful*, not hostile.      That’s the whole install.    # 8. How This Chapter Connects to the Rest of the Manual   From here, the documentation will branch:     -   **Manual** – how to operate Buddy day-to-day       - starting/stopping nodes     - reading monitors     - responding to alerts     - adjusting thresholds        -   **Product Guide** – what Buddy-based products can do for you       - example use cases     - configuration profiles     - role dashboards        -   **Fullerene Selector Guide** – for engineers and designers       - defining facets     - weighting values     - tuning selection behavior        -   **Monitor & Analysis Guide** – for analysts, ethics, and ops       - reading event traces     - understanding decisions     - reviewing “why” with clear language           All of them assume this chapter as the shared starting point:     - Buddy lives somewhere.   - You care about something.   - Both Sides Win is the rule.      Everything else is just: *how that looks from your side of the glass.*    # 9.
